## 2026-07-26 - PGEN-LANG-CAPABILITY-AUDIT-0011 (leaf `LANG-CAPABILITY-AUDIT.9`) — rule-definition uniqueness across a composed grammar, and the shipped multi-clause idiom finally documented

**Code change.** `rust/src/ebnf_frontend.rs` + two grammar-author book chapters. No release,
schema, ledger or contract movement.

Director ruling, verbatim: *"when loading a given EBNF file, any rule definition shall be unique
and any rule reference shall have one and only one rule definition."* That answers the
error-vs-warning question `.7` left open: **error**, and the "deliberate override" idiom is
rejected — there is no override mechanism.

**The measurement that shaped the fix.** Enforcing uniqueness per rule *header* would have
hard-failed two shipped grammars on the first load. Repeating a header is an existing, working
PGEN idiom: the clauses merge into alternatives of one rule (`start := "a"` + `start := "b"`
produces two raw_ast entries and `--lint-grammar` reports **1 rule**). `grammars/json.ebnf` uses
seven `value :=` clauses so each alternative carries its own return annotation, and
`grammars/rtl_const_expr.ebnf` writes its precedence cascade the same way. Those clauses are one
definition written across several lines, so the director's invariant already holds for them.

=> **The unit of uniqueness is the FILE, not the clause.** `register_rule_definitions` records
the distinct rule names each file defines and rejects a name already owned by a different file,
threaded through the whole composed graph at load. Zero risk to single-file grammars by
construction: the check can only fire when two distinct files are involved. The diagnostic names
the rule and **both** files.

**The idiom was documented nowhere** — the book's only mention of repeated rule names was the
includes chapter calling it a "well-formedness concern", i.e. describing a shipped, load-bearing
feature as a problem. `rules-and-expressions.md` gains a **Multi-clause definition** section, and
`includes.md` now states the actual hard-error contract with the quoted diagnostic and an explicit
"there is deliberately no override mechanism".

**Verified.** Driver extended to **22 declared-verdict cases, exit 0, 0 divergences**: cross-file
collision exit 1 naming both files; within-file multi-clause still merges to 1 rule; json.ebnf 9
and rtl_const_expr.ebnf 48 unchanged; a diamond does not false-positive. Blast radius was measured
before the change rather than assumed — every tracked grammar was re-scanned through the real
frontend, and only json, rtl_const_expr and the throwaway scratch slot carry repeats, all
within-file. clippy strict source 0 errors and 0 hits on the changed file;
`ebnf_frontend_dual_run_gate` GREEN (ebnf 131/131); `ebnf_parser_book_gate` GREEN; 9/9 doctrines.

**The one open reading — CLOSED by the director, same session.** The leaf shipped with one
question routed rather than absorbed: under a literal reading of the ruling, the within-file
idiom would also be forbidden, meaning two shipped grammars rewritten into `|` chains with
return-annotation and AST-shape risk. The director confirmed the reading taken here, verbatim:
*"You are right, I forgot this `RuleA := Branch_A | Branch_B | Branch_C` is the same as 3 rules
productions like `RuleA := Branch_A` then `RuleA := Branch_B` and `RuleA := Branch_C`"* => no
follow-up leaf, no grammar rewritten, file-scoped uniqueness is the complete enforcement. Note
that the question arose only because the idiom was documented nowhere — even its author needed
reminding it existed, which is the strongest case for the book section this leaf adds.

## 2026-07-26 - PGEN-LANG-CAPABILITY-AUDIT-0010 (leaf `LANG-CAPABILITY-AUDIT.7`) — include() reinstated for every EBNF consumer, and the detection failure root-caused

**Code change.** `rust/src/ebnf_frontend.rs` (include resolution) + `grammars/ebnf.ebnf` (a
stale dangling directive removed). No release, schema, ledger or contract movement — the
frontend composes rules *before* codegen, so no shipped parser's AST changes.

Director-ordered, in two parts: *"The linter should honour EBNF include() graph trees, of
course"*, then *"Full support for include() must be reinstated for every logic that consume
EBNF, not sure why this wasn't detected earlier and acted upon."*

**The fix — one chokepoint.** `ebnf_frontend.rs` exposes exactly two public functions and every
EBNF consumer goes through them (CLI codegen/lint/stimuli/raw-AST, the stimuli generator, the
parse-harness interpreter, the equivalence suite). Resolution was placed in
`parse_ebnf_text_to_raw_ast_envelope` above `scan_top_level_rules`, so no caller can opt out.
Rules are spliced, not text, so a trailing annotation in one file cannot bind the first rule of
the next; main-file rules stay first so an included file can never silently re-root the grammar.
Search path: including file's dir -> its includers' dirs -> `EBNF_INCLUDES` -> `EBNFLIB` -> `.`.
Two deliberate departures from the Perl behaviour: the including file's own directory is now
actually on the search path, and **an unresolvable include is a hard, named error** instead of a
silent no-op.

**`grammars/ebnf.ebnf:18` removed on measurement** — `grammars/semantic_annotations.ebnf` has
never existed, the grammar lints `undefined_references=0` without it, and composing in the real
`semantic_annotation.ebnf` would collide on 15 rule names.

**The reason nothing caught this — three independent maskings, all measured.** The
`ebnf_frontend_dual_run_diff_gate` diffs Perl against Rust on `ebnf`/`json`/`regex` and is exactly
the instrument for a dropped include. It stayed green because (1) the include target did not
exist, so Perl contributed zero rules too — **a dangling include masked a dropped include**;
(2) Perl's CLI passes no base directory, so even a valid target would not have resolved (its own
trace prints the search path as `<EBNF_INCLUDES>, .`); (3) the grammar actually being destroyed,
`systemverilog_lrm_profiled_wrapper.ebnf`, has **zero consumers** in any gate. And no gate
anywhere loaded a multi-file grammar — the include system had no positive test at all.

=> **A differential gate proves that two implementations AGREE, never that either is RIGHT.**
Banked in the horizon record.

**Verified.** `run_include_resolution_probes.sh` — 17 declared-verdict cases, exit 0, 0
divergences: two-file compose 1->**2** rules with `undefined_references` 1->**0** (the linter now
honours the graph and the misattributed "likely a typo" is gone with its cause); SV profiled
wrapper **3 -> 1403** rules; unresolvable include exit **0 -> 1**; cycle terminates; diamond
composes once; depth-3 + bare spec + relative subdir; `include_dir()` alphabetical; entry rule
pinned; all four consumer surfaces re-measured. No regression: five no-include grammars pinned
unchanged. The meta-grammar edit is **codegen-inert, proven byte-identical against a real HEAD
baseline with input AND output paths pinned** (sha256 `c0f26ff7...`, 156,863 lines).
`ebnf_frontend_dual_run_gate` GREEN at 131/131 Perl-vs-Rust parity on `ebnf`;
`ebnf_parser_book_gate` GREEN; clippy strict source **0 errors, 0 hits on the changed file**;
all 9 doctrines PASS.

**Left open and named:** cross-file rule-name collisions still resolve silently — new leaf `.9`,
which also carries a design call (a deliberate override may be a legitimate idiom, so
error-vs-warning is not obvious).

## 2026-07-26 - PGEN-LANG-CAPABILITY-AUDIT-0009 (leaf `LANG-CAPABILITY-AUDIT.4`) — pricing the roadmap re-measured the matrix, and two "gaps" turned out to be SHIPPED capabilities

**Docs-only.** Every probe grammar and every generated parser lived in a `mktemp -d` the driver
removes on exit. No Rust, no codegen, no generated artifact, no contract and no tracked grammar
was touched; no release, schema or ledger movement.

`.4` was meant only to *price* the gaps `.3`/`.3b` had already classified. Applying the
DESIGN-PRIOR-ART doctrine's **RE-MEASURE before citing engine behaviour** clause to each row
before ranking it moved **four of sixteen rows** — and two of them are not gaps at all.

**⛔ Row 15 (grammar composition) is a REGRESSION, not a gap.** `include()` ships, is recognized
(`ebnf_frontend.rs:246`) and is then silently discarded (`:152-155` — `idx += 1; continue`). A
two-file probe loads **1 rule with the included rule absent, exit 0, zero diagnostics**. The
capability was *implemented* in the retired Perl frontend (`perl/AST/Transform.pm:3234`) and is
documented as working by a whole chapter of the shipped, gated grammar-author book. Measured
damage on tracked grammars: `systemverilog_lrm_profiled_wrapper.ebnf` loads **3 of 1400 rules
(99.8% lost)**, and `grammars/ebnf.ebnf:18` carries `include(semantic_annotations)` pointing at
a file that **does not exist** — undetectable precisely because the directive never resolves.
The linter then reports the missing rules as *"UNDEFINED … likely a typo"*, blaming an innocent
rule. ⭐ **Director ruling (verbatim): "The linter should honour EBNF include() graph trees, of
course."** ⇒ includes are made real and the linter resolves the include graph — new leaf `.7`.

**⛔ Row 6 (error recovery) — "NOT yet in PGEN" was wrong; recovery SHIPS.** It exists as
registered semantic directives `@recover`/`@sync`/`@panic_until` plus three budgets
(`semantic_directive_registry.rs:253/269/273`), consumed by `rule_recovery_hints`
(`ast_based_generator.rs:9505`) into an emitted `parser.recover_with_hints(...)` call
(`:4222-4257`). **And `@recover: true` crashes codegen.** Root-caused from the emitted token
dump: the three `Option<usize>` budgets are interpolated straight into `quote!`, which emits
nothing for `None`, producing `recover_with_hints("stmt", parse_start, &[], &[], , , ,)` and
*"expected an expression"* at byte 0. Five-cell control matrix: `@recover` alone FAIL, +1 budget
FAIL, +all three OK — new leaf `.8`.

**⛔ Row 1 (parameterized productions) is worse than unwired.** `expr[In, Yield]` compiles to
`expr (In Yield)?` — an optional group — and **lints clean**, because `[` is the optional-element
form. The audit's highest-value declared surface is ambiguous by construction with a core
existing one.

**⚠️ Row 5 (case-insensitive keywords) is expressible today**, at 69 hand-written `(?i:...)`
across 216 rules in `grammars/vhdl.ebnf` — an ergonomic gap, not an expressive one. The declared
`~i"begin"` alternative misparses.

**⭐⭐ The unifying law: a name census is not a capability inventory.** The audit had been ranking
on consumer counts for meta-grammar production *names*, and this leaf measured that count lying
in both directions — false negative (every recovery production reads 0 while the capability
ships under other names) and false positive (`parameter_list` 2, `named_capture` 29 on substring
grep; both 0 word-anchored). `.3`'s "7 of 16 declared-unwired is the dominant class" is retracted.

**✅ The zero-cost acceptance test, measured rather than asserted.** A non-recovering parser
emits the recovery helper with **0 call sites**; `generated/json_parser.rs` carries **0 store
hits across 13,707 lines**. Both P0/P1 families inherit "non-users pay zero" by construction.

**The roadmap.** P0-1 include + linter graph → P0-2 `@recover` codegen fix → P1-3 fact
retraction / instance-scoped lifetime → P1-4 declarative case-insensitivity → P2-5 parameterized
productions (blocked on a surface call) → P2-6 cross-rule precedence → P2-7 offside + lexer modes
→ P3-8 NFKC → T-9 orphan report. Extensibility, row-16 mutable grammars and the three misparsing
declared syntaxes are recorded as deliberate exclusions.

**Declared scope exception.** The author book's include chapter and `docs/EBNF_INCLUDE_SYSTEM.md`
state a measured-false claim about a shipped, gated surface. Leaving them until `.7` lands would
be exactly the book drift the director forbids, so both gained a dated status admonition whose
removal is part of `.7`'s definition of done.

**Verification.** `run_primitive_pricing_probes.sh` — exit 0, 0 declared-verdict divergences,
byte-identical on re-run. `ebnf_parser_book_gate` GREEN (tracked HTML re-rendered). All 9
doctrines PASS. Clippy N/A (no Rust or generated-Rust file changed).

## 2026-07-26 - PGEN-LANG-CAPABILITY-AUDIT-0005 (leaf `LANG-CAPABILITY-AUDIT.5`) — the two measured doc defects repaired, and the mandated sweep found a third that fails SILENTLY

**Doc-surface only.** `grammars/ebnf.ebnf` is edited, but only inside a comment block: the
regenerated `ebnf` parser is **byte-identical** with both input and output paths pinned
(sha256 `f56f907556e8e27c07c7fcd45749b83581a5b427070f636f2de9d35a1694342c`), so the change is
codegen-inert. No release, schema, ledger or contract movement.

**⭐ The sweep came first, and it reframed the defects.** `.3b` found one bad book sentence and
one bad grammar example. Fixing them is worthless if the same claim is repeated elsewhere, so
the whole documentation surface was swept before anything was edited. Result: `parse-harness.md`
(the per-policy row table), `grammar-wellformedness.md` (which already carries a 2026-07-05
correction retracting the "PEG commits to the first success" reasoning) and — most importantly —
the grammar-author's own `docs/ebnf_parser_book/src/rules-and-expressions.md` were **already
correct**. So `developer-architecture.md:21` was the **sole outlier**, and the meta-grammar's
comment block was contradicting the very book PGEN ships for grammar authors.

**⛔ The third defect, found by that sweep, is the worst of the three.** Every one of the
documentation block's 15 example lines was run through `--lint-grammar` rather than eyeballed:

```
  LINT-FAIL  letter  := [a-zA-Z]        undefined rule 'Z' (+2 more) — hard error
  LINT-FAIL  special := [!@#$%^&*()]    hard error
  LINT-OK    digit   := [0-9]           ⚠️ and LINT-OK is the problem
```

`digit := [0-9]` lints clean and compiles to `Quantified{ element: Sequence{[]}, quantifier: "?" }`
— **an always-succeeding empty optional that matches nothing.** `[ … ]` is the optional-element
form (`ebnf.ebnf:288`), so a reader copying the documented character-class syntax gets a hard
error twice and a silently-vacuous rule once. The other 12 lines measured correct.

**The three edits.**

- `docs/book/src/developer-architecture.md` — the PEG bullet now says PGEN takes PEG's
  *determinism* property but **selects the winner by a branch tournament, not first-match
  commit**; it names the default `longest_match`, the `@branch_policy: ordered` opt-in and the
  measured `"a" | "a" "b"` / `"ab"` discriminator, keeps the (correct) greedy/possessive-repetition
  and `&`/`!` claims, and records why the distinction is load-bearing — two `--lint-grammar`
  deadness verdicts were unsound until they were made policy-conditional for exactly this reason.
- `grammars/ebnf.ebnf` — `@precedence: {level: 5, associativity: "left"}` (a payload the
  validator rejects) becomes `@precedence: 5` + `@associativity: left`; the character-class
  examples become regex atoms (`/[a-zA-Z]/`, `/[0-9]/`, `/[!@#$%^&*()]/`) with the bare-bracket
  trap spelled out, including the silent `[0-9]` case.
- `docs/ebnf_parser_book/src/quantifiers.md` — new section **"Repetition is POSSESSIVE — a
  quantifier never gives an iteration back"**: the measured `bt := "a"* "ab"` rejection, the rule
  *never write `body* closer` where `body` can match `closer`*, and both working idioms (static
  negative-lookahead guard; the semantic-store guard when the closer is only known at parse
  time), with `.3b`'s monotone-store bound stated up front so nobody adopts the second idiom
  without knowing it.

**⚠️ A no-regression measurement of ours was wrong, and the tool caught it.** The first run
reported the regenerated parser as DIVERGED across 12,224 lines. It had not diverged: the two
artifacts were generated to *different* `--output` paths and codegen embeds the output path in
the emitted source. Re-run with both the input path (`git stash` the edit in place) and the
output path held constant, the result is byte-identical. Recorded rather than quietly corrected —
it is the same trap `BIN-BUILD-INTEGRITY.3` already named, and a byte-identity claim is worthless
unless every non-semantic input is pinned.

**⭐ New leaf `.6` — a THIRD deadness class.** The third defect's deeper question is routed, not
absorbed: `character_class` (`ebnf.ebnf:232`) is **reachable, referenced and lint-clean**, and
still has zero implementing consumers — all 14 `character_class` hits in `rust/src` belong to the
*regex* grammar's class surface. The authoritative hand-written frontend lowers `[` to the
optional form instead, so the meta-grammar and the shipping frontend disagree about what `[ … ]`
means and the disagreement resolves silently. That is distinct from `.1`'s unreachable orphans
and `.2`'s unreferenced roots, and it belongs to the family `ANNOTATION-PLACEMENT` named: **a
check that cannot see a defect class must say so, not return green.**

**Verification.** Regenerated `ebnf` parser byte-identical (paths pinned); edited meta-grammar
lints clean (0 errors, the 2 pre-existing left-recursion `[info]` lines unchanged); the three
corrected character-class examples now lint OK; `mdbook_docs_gate` GREEN; `ebnf_parser_book_gate`
GREEN with the tracked HTML re-rendered; all 9 doctrines PASS. Clippy not applicable — no Rust or
generated-Rust file changed (proven by the byte-identity check).

## 2026-07-26 - PGEN-LANG-CAPABILITY-AUDIT-0004 (docs-only, read-only leaf `LANG-CAPABILITY-AUDIT.3b`) — the audit's six UNMEASURED rows are measured, and TWO "suspected gaps" turn out to be capabilities PGEN already has

**No code, grammar, generated artifact, contract or schema touched.** The scratch slot
(`grammars/scratch/scratch.ebnf`, the blessed throwaway probe grammar) is overwritten while the
driver runs and RESTORED by its `trap` on every exit path.

**Why the leaf existed.** `.3` shipped a 16-row cross-language capability matrix and marked six
rows ❓ UNMEASURED, explicitly forbidding anyone from citing them as fact. Two of those rows —
Raku-style user-chosen delimiters and here-documents — were logged as *suspected gaps* and would
have entered `.4`'s primitive roadmap as work items.

**Method.** Two probe banks (one per grammar-level layout policy) driven through the PARSE-HARNESS
**scratch slot** — authoritative *by construction*, since it runs the real register → codegen →
drive pipeline. Each row parsed in isolation via `--entry-rule`, so the banks' top-level
alternation cannot launder one row's verdict into another's. **43 cases, each with its required
verdict declared in the driver**, so a gap prints as `⛔` rather than being read out of prose.

**⭐⭐ Rows 10 and 11 are NOT gaps.** The open delimiter set is expressible today with a
store-driven dynamic guard — register the opening delimiter with `@emit_fact`, gate every body
element `lacks_fact` against it, gate the closer `has_fact`:

```
  ACCEPT  q/abc/   ACCEPT  q!abc!   ACCEPT  q#abc#   ACCEPT  q/ab!c/   ACCEPT  q//
  REJECT  q/abc!                                        (closer must equal opener)
```

and the same construction gives a correct here-document **including the case that separates a real
heredoc from a hack** — a body line that looks like a *different* tag:

```
  ACCEPT  <<END\nline1\nEOF\nline2\nEND\n      REJECT  <<EOF\nline1\n   (unterminated)
```

**⭐⭐ The real bound is fact LIFETIME — one named primitive, not a lexical-layer family.** Both
rows fail identically once a *second* quote/heredoc appears: the first instance's delimiter fact is
still live, so it blocks a legal body character and closes the wrong quote. Root-caused to four
source facts — the only negative query is the parse-global `lacks_fact`
(`semantic_runtime.rs:3963`); there is no `lacks_fact_in_current_scope` and no fact-retraction
directive (both measured at 0 occurrences); `close_scope` pops the chain but never retracts
(`:2852`, `:6152`); and the scope-local index is keyed by scope **depth**, not identity (`:2170`),
so sibling instances collide anyway. The `@open_scope`/`@close_scope` repair was **built and
measured**, not assumed: its verdicts are byte-for-byte the unscoped ones.

⇒ this **half-refutes `.3`'s own hypothesis** that rows 2/3/4/10/11 all need "parse state feeding
the lexical layer". Rows 10 and 11 need no new lexical channel — the store already steers the
lexical decision. Recorded as a correction rather than smoothed over.

**The other four verdicts.** Row 8 (contextual/soft keywords) ✅ **HAVE, and with no
keyword-exclusion tax** — all three readings of Python's `match` parse against a deliberately
un-taxed identifier token. Row 9 (cover grammars / delayed disambiguation) ✅ **HAVE**, including a
disambiguator sitting past an arbitrarily deep ambiguous prefix. Row 12 confirmed and sharpened:
`@priority`/`@precedence` take an **integer** payload and rank alternatives **inside one rule** —
there is no cross-rule precedence ladder. Row 13 split: ✅ Unicode classes work
(`\p{XID_Start}`/`\p{XID_Continue}` compile and discriminate) / ❌ NFKC normalization is absent
(0 normalization crates, 0 NFKC/NFC/NFD mentions in `rust/src`).

**⭐ A general engine law the matrix never named: quantifiers are POSSESSIVE.** `"a"* "ab"` rejects
both `ab` and `aaab` — the loop never gives an iteration back. Trace-confirmed and located at
`generate_quantified_logic` (`ast_based_generator.rs:5692`). This is consistent with the design
(the book already says PGEN has "greedy/possessive repetition"), but it is why the naive
`body* close` delimiter shape cannot work, and the author-facing consequence — write
`(!close body)* close`, and reach for the store guard when `close` is not static — is documented
nowhere. Both idioms measured working.

**⚠️ TWO doc surfaces measured WRONG, routed to a new leaf `.5` rather than fixed inline.**
`docs/book/src/developer-architecture.md:21` says *"PGEN is a faithful PEG: **ordered choice**,
`&`/`!`, greedy quantifiers"* — the greedy half is right, the ordered-choice half is measurably
false for the default policy (`a | a b` on `"ab"`: default ACCEPTs, `@branch_policy: ordered`
REJECTs, and `--lint-grammar` independently flags the shadowing on the `ordered` rule only). And
`grammars/ebnf.ebnf:688`, inside the meta-grammar's own documentation-examples block, advertises
`@precedence: {level: 5, associativity: "left"}` — a payload the validator rejects, pinned by the
engine's own test `semantic_validator_warns_on_invalid_priority_payload` (re-run this session:
PASS). That is `.1`'s decorative-surface disease landing in the examples an author copies.

**Verification.** 43/43 cases through the real pipeline; **10 printed `⛔` gaps, all inside the two
named families and none elsewhere**; the whole set re-runnable by one command
(`docs/tasks/artifacts/lang_capability_audit/run_capability_probes.sh`, exit 0). All 9 enforced
doctrines PASS. Nothing shipped was touched, so there is no release, schema or ledger movement.

## 2026-07-26 - PGEN-LEX-ADJACENCY-0001 (docs-only, read-only design leaf `LEX-ADJACENCY.1`) — the "missing" no-layout primitive is not missing: it ships on BOTH halves and no grammar can ask for it

**No code, grammar, generated artifact, contract or schema touched** — the leaf is read-only
plus a design record. It closes the design leaf the previous slice opened, and it **corrects
one of that slice's findings**.

**⭐ The finding.** `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.11` concluded "ROUTE 4 — a generator-side 'no layout
here' primitive ⛔ DOES NOT EXIST". Measured this session, on both sides of the engine, that
is wrong — the capability exists and ships; what is absent is any way for a **grammar** to
request it:

- **PARSE.** `match_regex(pattern, /*skip_leading_whitespace=*/ false)` is live and emitted:
  `generated/return_annotation_parser.rs` uses it at **10 of its 20** `match_regex` sites. It
  is gated by a hard-coded rule-NAME `matches!` arm naming exactly `string_content_double` /
  `string_content_single` (`ast_based_generator.rs:5551`, five mirrors in
  `cascade.rs`/`cascade/value.rs`/`scan.rs`, plus the census constant
  `fusibility_census.rs:60`). SystemVerilog's `0 of 1,798` — the number `.3.11` measured
  correctly — is simply because no SV rule carries one of those two names. ⚠️ That name-gate
  is itself an `EBNF-SOURCE-OF-TRUTH` breach (an acceptance-affecting rule-name literal
  inside the engine), so retiring it is a doctrine win independent of the SV defect.
- **GENERATE.** Interior separator suppression is live as `atomic_token_depth`, but it is
  **inferred** from the return shape (`rule_is_lexically_atomic`, `stimuli_generator.rs:13023`:
  a `-> $text`/`$0` return on every branch, or a `@transform` directive) — never something a
  grammar states on purpose.

**⭐ The gap, measured as a 2×2 rather than an absence.** Probes at seed 0
(`docs/tasks/artifacts/lex_adjacency/run_probes.sh`):

| setting | interior seam | exterior seam | emitted |
|---|---|---|---|
| ordinary object return (today's `time_literal`) | open ✗ | separated ✓ | `<A>timeunit 0 ns;` |
| `-> $text` (inferred atomic) | closed ✓ | fused ✗ | `<D>timeunit02s;` |
| `@transform` (inferred atomic) | closed ✓ | fused ✗ | `E0105fs` |
| **what IEEE 1800-2017 fn 44 requires** | closed ✓ | separated ✓ | `timeunit 10ns;` |

The fourth row is unreachable because `stimuli_generator.rs:9421` derives both effects from a
single `is_atomic` bool — **while `append_generated_segment` already consumes them as two
independent conditions**. The fused row is not merely ugly: `/timeunit\b/` cannot be followed
by a digit, so `<D>timeunit02s;` does not re-parse; it would trade one duality break for
another.

**The decision.** A rule-level **`@lexical_token: true`** semantic annotation — *"this rule
denotes one lexical token"* — **deep** (transitive over the rule's derivation) and
**interior-only** (the rule's own outer boundaries keep separating normally). The inferred
`$text`/`@transform` atomicity keeps its exterior-fusing behaviour, which is correct for the
token **fragments** it was built for (`"R"` + `digits` → `R12`), so the two use-cases stay
distinguishable and regex/VHDL carry no regression risk.

Rejected on measurement, not taste:

- a **sequence-level** adjacency operator (`a . b`) — per-element annotations are not
  generator-visible today, so it needs a whole new annotation-visibility tier for no
  expressive gain on any known consumer;
- a **runtime** depth counter for the parse half — it would tax all 1,798 terminal sites for
  a primitive used by two rules, which the ⭐ speed north star forbids. The parse half is
  therefore emitted **statically** (specialized no-layout twins over the annotated rule's
  closure), and its affordability was measured rather than assumed: `time_literal`'s
  transitive closure is **14 of 1,475 rules (<1%)**, via the new `closure_probe.py` reading
  the `--dump-gen-ast` IR that codegen itself consumes.

**⭐ The tree's certificate condition is discharged in advance.** `.3.11`'s `@sample` route
died because pinning the only path to `time_unit` collapsed generator coverage to **rules
3/13, branches 0/6**, stranding seven rules toward cert `UNKNOWN`. The atomic route holds
**rules 11/11, branches 5/5** — every unit branch still generated. That contrast is what makes
this route viable where the previous one was not.

**⚠️ Two traps named before implementation, not discovered after.** (1) The parse half must
also drop **explicit** layout: SV writes `kw_ns_7320d5b7 := trivia /ns\b/`
(`systemverilog.ebnf:6458`), so flipping `skip_leading_whitespace` alone would still accept
`10 ns`. (2) "Deep" closes seams some LRM productions deliberately leave **open** — IEEE
1800-2017 §5.7.1, the law `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.10` established, permits white space at a based
literal's size↔apostrophe and base↔value seams; `time_literal` is safe only because A.8.4
restricts its number to `unsigned_number`/`fixed_point_number`, so the footnote 33/48/50
re-sweep must be per-rule, never mechanical.

**Evidence** (`docs/tasks/artifacts/lex_adjacency/`): two probe grammars, two re-runnable
drivers, two captured outputs — both drivers `cmp`-clean on re-run. Design record:
`docs/tasks/LEX-ADJACENCY-design.md`. Frontier moves to `LEX-ADJACENCY.2`, which should
convert `return_annotation.ebnf` first — its `no-skip=10 of 20` is the migration's own
regression test. The book chapter `docs/book/src/lexical-annotations.md` documents the
inferred form today and is a declared `.2` obligation, deliberately deferred: publishing an
annotation the engine does not yet accept would be book drift.

## 2026-07-26 - PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0028 (docs-only; leaf SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.11 DIAGNOSED + fix WRITTEN and PARSER-VERIFIED but DELIBERATELY NOT LANDED; new tree LEX-ADJACENCY) — the `time_literal` defect is TWICE what the charter said, and its fix is blocked by a MISSING PGEN PRIMITIVE, measured on both sides of the engine

**No release, schema or ledger bump: the grammar is back at HEAD.** This slice ships
diagnosis, a fully verified (and then reverted) fix, a measured design adjudication, a new
capability tree, and one toolbox correction.

**⭐ The charter understated the defect by a whole direction.** `time_literal := number
time_unit` (`:495`) was chartered as an accepts-invalid nicety with "zero measured
conflict". It is also a **rejects-valid defect that breaks legal real-world code**: because
`s`/`ms`/`us`/`ns`/`ps`/`fs` are ordinary identifier spellings, the over-permissive rule
STEALS the ubiquitous `<number> <white space> <signal>` pair. `#1 ps[idx] = 1'b1;`
(iverilog), `#2 s = ~s;` (Surelog) and `a ##1 s ##1 b` (ispras ×2) all REJECT today, and two
of those four files are tracked `divergence:unexplained_rejects_valid` rows. Trace-proven:
`Rule 'time_literal' successfully parsed from 48 to 51 (consumed 3 bytes: '2 s')`. A second
independent face was found too: IEEE 1800-2017 A.8.4 restricts the number to
`unsigned_number`/`fixed_point_number`, but the rule referenced the full A.8.7 `number`, so
`timeunit 1e3ns;`, `1.5e3ns`, `4'd10ns` and `'d10ns` all wrongly ACCEPT.

**The fix was written and measured PERFECT on the parser** — a positive lookahead on the
fused lexeme, keeping `number time_unit` structural. All **38** matrix rows exactly as
designed; the `{value, unit}` AST object byte-identical; census byte-inert (1475→1475,
per-rule profile map identical across all 1475 rules); main corpus **pass 9,693 → 9,698 with
0 pass→fail**, **rejects-valid 382 → 380** (both healed rows the keyed files, zero new),
accepts-invalid 21 set-identical; `verilog_2005` lane 0 transitions with a byte-identical
manifest; `sv_syntax_closure_gate` PASS; `ast_shape_contract_gate` PASS 18/18.

**⛔ And then it was reverted, because `sv_cert_recognized_union_gate` went RED on a
GEN↔PARSE DUALITY BREAK** — `sample_parse_failures` 22/16/17 at seeds 0/7/42 (expected 0).
The certificate accounting stayed perfect; the generator simply emits samples the strict
parser rejects (`timeprecision 0//x\n//x\nps;`).

**⭐ The deciding measurement — three grammar shapes, one generator run.** `num unit` with
`trivia`-prefixed unit tokens emits `A 7904 ns`; the SAME structure with `trivia` REMOVED
still emits `B 8918 s`; only a single fused terminal emits the tight `C 19.20808ns`. ⇒ **the
generator inserts a separator between EVERY pair of sequence elements, and PGEN cannot
express "no layout between these two elements".** IEEE 1800-2017 Annex A footnotes 33/48/50
are satisfied today only because their constructs happen to collapse into one token
(measured 15/15 correct); footnote 44 is the one that cannot, because the LRM also names
`time_unit ::= s | ms | us | ns | ps | fs`.

**All four routes measured, each blocked:** (1) lookahead — generator breaks; (2) fused
terminal — duality-complete but orphans `time_unit` **and its 6 `kw_*` tokens**, an Annex-A
production that `feedback_no_rule_deletion_without_lrm_proof` forbids deleting and the
lint/closure gates forbid leaving unreferenced, and it flattens `{value, unit}` (a regex
terminal binds exactly one value — codegen has no capture-group → `$N` mapping); (3)
`@sample: "10ns"` generator pin — measured to pin correctly, but as the sole path to
`time_unit` it collapses generator coverage to **rules 3/13, branches 0/6**; (4) a no-layout
primitive — does not exist (all 1,798 `match_regex` call sites pass
`skip_leading_whitespace = true`).

**⛔ Nothing was degraded to make a gate pass.** No LRM rule deleted, no cert contract
re-baselined to absorb a duality break, no schema broken, no gate re-specified. Grammar,
`ast_shape_contract.rs` and the corpus characterization outputs are all restored to HEAD, the
parser regenerated from the restored grammar, and all three binaries rebuilt against it.

**New tree `LEX-ADJACENCY`** owns the enabling primitive: a NO-LAYOUT lexical boundary that
BOTH the parser and the stimuli generator honour. Two independent families now need it —
this leaf, and the `rtl_frontend.ebnf:375` note that recorded the parse half in 2026 and
called it "a future parser-agnostic capability".

**Toolbox correction landed (independent of the block).** `TOOLBOX.md` §2.2: `--trace-rules R`
traces R's **dynamic extent**, so naming a suspect leaf rule alone can print NOTHING while
that rule succeeds — measured (`time_literal` alone → 0 lines; its caller `cycle_delay_range`
→ the line that is the whole root cause). ⚠️ This retro-weakens one leg of `.3.10`'s jitter
argument, which used trace-emptiness as proof of non-entry: `--dump-rule-entry-counts-json`
shows `time_literal` entered **28,643** times on the very file `.3.10` reasoned about.

## 2026-07-25 - PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0025 (leaf SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.10 DONE, release 1.0.175->1.0.176, schema 19 UNCHANGED, ledger SV-0046) — the SPACED UDP / timing-check NUMBER literals (`1 'b 1`) were ABSENT, and the spaced timing-check constant silently DEGRADED its AST shape; both restored + the fused number-literal class swept EXHAUSTIVELY

Session #206. Opened by `.3.9`'s WIDENED sweep, not by a corpus row — and that origin is the point: the corpus never tripped this defect, and still does not. This is the first leaf in the `.3.x` series whose entire value is LRM fidelity rather than graduation yield, and it is presented as such rather than dressed up.

**Root cause.** IEEE 1800-2017 **§5.7.1** (verbatim) says a based literal "shall be composed of up to three tokens" — an optional size, an apostrophe followed by a base format character, and the value — and then fixes exactly which interior seams may carry white space: **size↔apostrophe OPEN** (separate lexical tokens, §5.3, no carve-out), **apostrophe↔base-char CLOSED** ("shall *not* be separated by any white space"), **base_format↔value OPEN explicitly** ("The unsigned number token shall immediately follow the base format, *optionally preceded by white space*"). Release `1.0.171` (`SV-0041`, leaf `.3.5`) gave `integral_number:439` exactly those two seams. But `init_val:2554` (UDP initial value, A.5.2) and `scalar_constant:4935` (timing-check conditions, A.7.5.3) enumerate the LRM's **CLOSED literal set**, so they never route through `integral_number` — they carry **12 fused number-literal tokens of their own** (`1'b0`…`1'BX`, plus the unsized `'b0`/`'b1`/`'B0`/`'B1`) and never inherited the fix. A fused literal cannot admit interior white space: `trivia` runs only BEFORE a terminal, never inside one match — the same engine property `SV-0041` and `SV-0045` each root-caused.

**⭐ Tool-pinned differentially, and the trace showed something worse than a rejection.** On `1 'b 1` branches 1/2/5/6 fail on their contiguous regexes at the space before the `'`, branches 3/4/7/8 (string literals) fail likewise — and then **branch 9, the LRM's BARE `1` alternative, MATCHES**, so `longest_match` selects `9/10 consuming 2 chars`. `init_val` therefore **SUCCEEDS** having eaten only the `1`, and the parse dies DOWNSTREAM in `sequential_body` (surface 189, furthest 266). A mis-parse that reports its failure in a different rule is exactly why reading the error position would have sent an investigator to the wrong place — the case for TOOLBOX-first, not a formality. On the tight `1'b1` the SAME branch 2 matches and wins with 5 chars; only the whitespace differs.

**⭐ A SECOND FACE THE LEAF DID NOT KNOW ABOUT — `scalar_constant` never rejected, it silently DEGRADED the AST.** `scalar_timing_check_condition:4967` carries a fallback `expression` branch, so a failing `scalar_constant` never fails the file; it just loses the typed shape. Measured by AST dump: `cond == 1 'b 1` in a `specify` timing check produced the flat `{kind:"expression"}` where the tight form produced `{kind:"eq", lhs, rhs:{kind:"1'b1"}}`. This face is invisible to every pass/fail column in the corpus and would never have been found by another rejects-valid sweep. **Lesson banked: a rule with an expression-shaped fallback converts an acceptance defect into a shape defect, so "the corpus still passes" is not evidence that a construct works.**

**Fix (grammar-only; 12 token BODIES and nothing else):** `[ \t]*` at exactly the two §5.7.1-open seams — `/1[ \t]*'b[ \t]*0\b/` … for the 8 sized tokens, `/'b[ \t]*0\b/` … for the 4 unsized twins (which have only ONE interior seam, there being no size token). The 4 string-literal tokens became regexes **without** gaining a `\b` they never had, preserving their prefix-matching semantics exactly. ⭐ Keeping them as their own tokens rather than swapping in `integral_number` is what **keeps the closed set closed**: the leading `1` stays hard-coded, so `2'b11` still cannot be an `init_val` — the naive-swap trap the charter warned about, discharged by construction and verified by a negative control. `[ \t]` (horizontal) matches `.3.5` deliberately; a newline-spanning literal is the same deferred composite-rule case there and here. **No new rules or tokens — census 1475 UNCHANGED.** Cross-profile (IEEE 1364-2005 §3.5.1 is identical and these tokens carry no `@profiles` gate), so `verilog_2005` heals too — like `.3.5`, unlike the SVA-gated `.3.8`/`.3.9`.

**Verified (26-row matrix over BOTH consumer rules, same driver script re-run for before and after — not re-typed).** 8 rows REJECT→ACCEPT, identically under `verilog_2005`. **must-ACCEPT 16/16 and must-REJECT 9/9 under both profiles** — the over-permissiveness guard is measured, not argued, and includes the LRM-critical pair `1' b 1` / `1 ' b 1` which §5.7.1 PROHIBITS and which still reject, plus `2'b1`, `1'b2`, `1'bz`, `1'b 11` and the digit-less `1'b` (the `SV-0030` guard). **AST kinds BYTE-IDENTICAL tight vs spaced** — 4/4 pairs via `--entry-rule init_val`, only `span_end` differing — which proves both that the correct LRM alternative now wins instead of the bare-`1` fallback, and that no kind is renamed.

**⭐ The +0 corpus yield was DERIVED AND STATED BEFORE MEASURING.** The 12 tokens have exactly two context-restricted consumers (`init_val` UDP-only, `scalar_constant` timing-check-only). Of 16,336 files, 150 carry a spaced literal but only 3 also contain `primitive`/`specify` — and probing all 3 shows each dies elsewhere (`` `ifdef `` ×2, UDP-table edge symbols ×1). Keyed population **0 rows**, ceiling +0, measured +0. Main corpus: pass 9,694 → 9,693, **rejects-valid 382 → 382 SET-IDENTICAL**, accepts-invalid 21 SET-IDENTICAL, match 5,727 SET-IDENTICAL — the entire 16,336-row manifest differs by **exactly one line**. `verilog_2005` lane re-run (and here it HAD to be, since this fix genuinely reaches that profile): 2,459 files 2,180/279/0, **ZERO transitions**, manifest BYTE-IDENTICAL.

**⛔ NO REGRESSION — and the one jitter row was PROVEN, not argued.** The single `pass→timeout` (`verilator/test_regress/t/t_math_synmul_mul.v`) was dismissed by a stronger method than `.3.8`/`.3.9` used. Those leaves argued reachability from file TEXT ("contains no `##`"), which is an inference. Here it was measured with the instrument: `--trace-rules init_val,scalar_constant` emits **0** lines on that exact file while the SAME probe with the SAME flags emits **10** on the repro — so the zero is a real zero and the edited regexes are provably never executed there; the file contains `primitive` 0× and `specify` 0×; run solo it takes 17.9 s against the 20 s wall and exits 0 = **pass**; and `.3.9` recorded this SAME file flipping the OPPOSITE way. ⚠️ Its 15 s (`.3.9`) → 17.9 s (here) solo drift was explicitly NOT waved away — that is precisely the shape a silent speed regression would take against a fixed wall, and the north star makes speed co-equal and never-regressed. **⭐ The mandated sweep ran and is EXHAUSTIVE.** All **14** token definitions embedding an apostrophe were adjudicated (grammar-wide grep, no sampling): 12 = this defect; `tick := "'"` is one character so it has no interior; and **`unbased_unsized_literal:493` (`'0`/`'1`/`'x`/`'z`) ADJUDICATED CORRECT AS FUSED with a named LRM cause** — Annex A footnote **48**: *"The apostrophe ( ' ) in unbased_unsized_literal shall not be followed by white_space."* ⭐ **That is the sweep's most valuable outcome: this token looks structurally IDENTICAL to the defective unsized `'b0` twins, and a mechanical "add seams wherever there is an apostrophe" pass would have widened acceptance against the standard.** Same adjudication shape as `.3.9`'s `attr_open`/`attr_close`. The 7 neighbouring closed-literal-set rules (`edge_descriptor`, `level_symbol`, `output_symbol`, `zero_or_one`, `z_or_x`, `finish_number`, `1step`) were swept too — all one-character tokens or already-structural multi-token sequences, so no interior seam. **0 further members; the fused NUMBER-literal face of the class is CLOSED.**

**Gates (all GREEN, seeds 0/7/42), with BOTH cert contracts UNTOUCHED — the `.3.8` posture, PREDICTED IN WRITING BEFORE THE GATES RAN.** The prediction rested on a measured census: rule_count 1475→1475, satisfiable_under sv_2017 1352→1352 / sv_2023 1371→1371 / verilog_2005 1121→1121, and the strongest available form — **the per-rule profile map is identical across all 1475 rules (0 differences)**. `ast_shape_contract_gate` **18/18** (the decisive no-schema-bump proof: the three locked samples `init_val_lrm_digits` / `scalar_constant_lrm_digits` / `scalar_timing_check_condition_eq` pin exactly these kinds and pass unchanged). `sv_cert_recognized_union_gate` GREEN with **no re-baseline** (union_witness 1346 == expected, canonical UNKNOWN 11, union UNKNOWN 0, residual `[]`, `fully_certified_via_union`, spf=0, unmet 0). `verilog_2005_conformance_gate` GREEN **byte-inert** (cert `1121/328/779/14` as pinned, matrix 240 checks / 0 mismatches, aliases 2, orphans 0). `sv_syntax_closure_gate` PASS (1475 rules, 0 unreachable). `sv_external_corpus_triage_gate` PASS. `--lint-grammar` clean with `profile_orphans=0`. Clippy source-strict PASS with the generated stage at **291** = exactly the tracked baseline (zero new generated debt) — obtained with `PGEN_CLIPPY_FORCE=1`, re-confirming `.3.9`'s finding that the clippy step silently self-exempts on grammar-only leaves because `generated/` is gitignored. ⚠️ The recorded risk that a widened REGEX terminal could still move the witness column (the stimuli generator synthesizes witnesses FROM the regex) is exactly why both cert gates were run rather than argued away; measured outcome: the witness column did not move. `sv_stimuli_quality_gate` PASS (guard exit 0, peak 11,967 MB / 1,993 s; profiles 2/2, `closed_loop_initial_replay_determinism_passes` 2/2, preprocess warnings 0 / errors 0, all 16 sample rows pass at 100% parseability acceptance). `systemverilog_parser_book_gate` PASS, with the rendered `changelog-index.html` VERIFIED to carry the new `1.0.176` entry rather than trusting the gate's "HTML present" check.

**⚠️⚠️ `closed_loop_replay_targets_total` 124 → 127 (+3) — NOT semantically attributable to this leaf, and chasing that down surfaced a MEASUREMENT-INTEGRITY problem in how the whole `.3.x` series reads this metric.** The gate passes either way; this is about what the number MEANS. **Measured:** all 127 targets were ENUMERATED (62 `sv_2017` + 65 `sv_2023`) and intersected with the changed surface — the 12 edited tokens plus the full consumer chain (`init_val`, `scalar_constant`, `scalar_timing_check_condition`, `sequential_body`, `udp_declaration_*`, `specify_block`) — and the **intersection is EMPTY in both profiles**, by rule name, node path, branch id and raw substring. Every one of the 23/24 distinct target rules is a constraint / assertion / class / property / net-declaration surface. **Ruled out:** it is not sampling noise — `SV-REPLAY-DEBT.1` verified determinism directly, two canonical runs at one vintage giving byte-identical gap artifacts (sha256, all four JSONs) — and not timeout pressure, since this run measured zero target and helper timeout errors. **Inferred (labelled as such):** the generator is seeded and deterministic *for a fixed grammar*, but widening a regex enlarges its generatable language and shifts the generator's consumption of the random stream, reshuffling which unrelated branches get witnessed inside the 5,000-attempt budget. ⛔ **The finding: five prior leaves narrated this metric causally without ever checking relatedness** — `.3.9` recorded "−3 = three replay-debt gaps CLOSED, moving toward `focused_replay_target_debt_zero`", `.3.8` "+1 = the bracketed alternative is a NEW generation target", and so on. Since `focused_replay_target_debt_zero` is the **LAST unmet SV family-status criterion**, a `Done` gate is being scored on a number that moves for unverified reasons. ## 2026-07-25 - PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0024 (leaf SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.9 DONE, release 1.0.174->1.0.175, schema 18->19, ledger SV-0045) — the SPACED SVA cycle-delay abbreviations `## [*]` / `## [+]` were ABSENT (four lexical tokens FUSED into one literal atom); restored + the fused-literal class swept EXHAUSTIVELY

Session #205. Not a fresh corpus cut: this leaf was opened by `.3.8`'s own measurement — the 1 keyed row of 24 that did NOT flip. `.3.8` root-caused that leftover instead of writing it off, which is the whole reason the defect is here rather than undiscovered.

**Root cause (the OPPOSITE face of `SV-0044`'s class).** IEEE 1800-2017 A.2.10's third and fourth `cycle_delay_range` alternatives were single FUSED literal tokens — `kw_token_71b8cf7e := trivia "##[*]"` (`grammars/systemverilog.ebnf:6655`) and `kw_token_9768502a := trivia "##[+]"` (`:6659`) — each fusing **four** distinct SystemVerilog lexical tokens (`##` + `[` + `*`/`+` + `]`), every one of which already exists standalone in this grammar and is used standalone elsewhere. A fused multi-character literal cannot admit interior white space (the `trivia` layout skipper runs only BEFORE a terminal, never inside one match — the same engine property `SV-0041` root-caused for spaced number literals). The governing law is IEEE 1800-2017 **§5.3**, verbatim: white space "shall be ignored **except when they serve to separate other lexical tokens**". So every spaced spelling is legal SystemVerilog, and every one of them rejected while the tight spelling parsed. Where `SV-0044` was A.2.10's brackets wrongly read as METASYNTAX, this is A.2.10's brackets wrongly FUSED into an atom — the two faces of the ledger's documented dropped-delimiter class.

**Tool-pinned DIFFERENTIALLY, not just as "the branch failed."** On the spaced input all four branches fail at the `##` position (`❌ Branch 3/4 for rule 'cycle_delay_range' failed at position 209`, bytes 209.. = `' ## [*] '`); on the tight input the SAME branch WINS (`🏁 Rule 'cycle_delay_range' selected branch 3/4 consuming 6 chars`). That isolates whitespace as the sole variable.

**Fix (grammar-only), reusing an in-grammar idiom rather than inventing one:** alternatives 3/4 become `kw_token_93ac8946 lbrack star rbrack -> {kind: "star"}` and `... lbrack plus rbrack -> {kind: "plus"}` (`:1707`/`:1709`), and the two fused tokens are RETIRED. `consecutive_repetition:1377` already spells exactly that shape for `[ * ]` / `[ + ]`, so the fix reuses existing tokens AND the house idiom, and the emitted kinds become the grammar's own vocabulary instead of two extractor hash artifacts. No new rules or tokens; census **1477 -> 1475**.

**⚠️ Schema 18 -> 19, decided ON MEASUREMENT (the charter required adjudicating this first).** The rename `{kind:"token_71b8cf7e"}` -> `{kind:"star"}` and `{kind:"token_9768502a"}` -> `{kind:"plus"}` is breaking for AST consumers. All 31 locked `ast_shape_contract` samples were machine-checked: ZERO reference these kinds (the only hits in that file are `calibration_history` prose). No LIVE normative contract table references them either — the two doc hits sit inside era-dated 1.0.77/1.0.54 release-highlight blocks, which correctly keep their historical wording (checked against `git show d0d2152f`: this is NOT a `.3.8` lockstep gap, as first suspected). BUT an AST dump proves both kinds were REACHABLE AND EMITTED, unlike `.3.8`'s unreachable `paren_range` — so a downstream consumer keyed on the old hash names would break, and that is exactly what the schema version exists to signal. Under-signalling a breaking rename to save a version number is the wrong trade.

**⭐ The mandated sweep ran, and was WIDENED past the charter's bracket filter.** §5.3 makes the real test "is this fused literal ONE lexical token, or several?" — not "does it contain a bracket". So all **52** multi-character literal token definitions were adjudicated, plus 48 inline-literal hits: **46 correct as fused** (single operator glyphs like `!=`, `<<<=`, `|->`); **2 ADJUDICATED CORRECT AS FUSED with a named LRM cause** — `attr_open "(*"` / `attr_close "*)"`, on the §5.4 `/*`-block-comment precedent, 36/36 LRM attribute examples written tight with zero spaced, and because un-fusing would collide with the LRM's own separate `event_control ::= ... | @ (*)` production (a speculative "fix" here would have changed acceptance with no LRM support); **2 = this defect**; and **0** fused grammar literals hiding in rule bodies (all 48 inline hits are `@sample:` payloads, `@fact_kind:` descriptions, comments, or regex-terminal bodies). **Measured globally (guarded, both lanes).** Repro: the charted 6-row matrix — `## [*]` and `## [+]` REJECT->ACCEPT, all four controls held. **The CLASS is closed, not just the two charted forms:** 9 spacing variants (`##[*]`, `## [*]`, `##[ *]`, `##[* ]`, `##  [  *  ]`, tab-separated, and the `+` twins) ALL ACCEPT. **Not over-permissive:** 5 near-miss negatives (`##[]`, `##[*`, `##[**]`, `##[+*]`, `##[1:2:3]`) ALL still REJECT. `verilog_2005` still rejects both spellings; AST confirmed `{kind:"star"}`/`{kind:"plus"}` with ZERO residual `token_*` kinds. ## 2026-07-25 - PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0023 (leaf SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.8 DONE, release 1.0.173->1.0.174, schema 18 UNCHANGED, ledger SV-0044) — the SVA bracketed cycle-delay range `##[m:n]` was ABSENT (literal LRM brackets read as EBNF optional-grouping); restored

Session #204. The sixth defect cut from the `.3` rejects-valid family map, picked on measurement: the map was refreshed at the current **406**-row baseline and ranked by *normalized stuck signature* (sharper than the coarse family bucket), which put `[ NUM :` on top at 28 rows across 3 suites — **24 of them carrying `##[`**. The largest homogeneous, 100%-LRM-legal, zero-adjudication-ambiguity pure-grammar gap remaining.

**Root cause (the SIXTH+ instance of an ALREADY-DOCUMENTED class).** IEEE 1800-2017 A.2.10 defines `cycle_delay_range ::= ## constant_primary | ## [ cycle_delay_const_range_expression ] | ##[*] | ##[+]`, where alternative 2's `[ ]` are **literal SystemVerilog brackets**. But the LRM's BNF meta-notation uses `[ ]` for *both* literal brackets and optional items — a distinction the published PDF carries typographically and the **PDF->text conversion destroys** — so the extractor emitted PGEN's optional-group metasyntax `( ... )?` (`grammars/systemverilog.ebnf:1705`). `##` was therefore followed by an *optional, bracket-less* range, and no alternative could consume the `[`: alt 1 needs a `constant_primary`, alt 2 took the empty option and left `[1:3]` to `seq_unary`, alts 3/4 require the exact literals. Bracketed cycle-delay ranges were **100% unparseable in every profile** while unbracketed `##1`/`##2` parsed fine — exactly the corpus split observed. Trace-proven, not inferred: `Leaving branch 2/4 for rule 'cycle_delay_range' at position 121 (success)` catches branch 2 succeeding on `##` alone at precisely the reported `furthest_position=121`. The LRM settles the reading in its **own prose** — "`##[*]` is used as an equivalent representation of `##[0:$]`" and "`##[+]` ... of `##[1:$]`", forms writable only if the brackets are literal — plus ~15 source examples. ⛔ **Correction of record, made before landing:** this is NOT a new class — the bug ledger already NAMES it *"the documented dropped-delimiter class"*, with at least five priors (`SV-0002` `stream_concatenation`'s `{ }`+`[ ]`, the covergroup `trans_range_list` repeats, the `boolean_abbrev` repetition family, the six covergroup-adjacent SVA bounded-property operators, and `value_range`). ⭐⭐ `boolean_abbrev` is in **A.2.10, the SAME Annex A subclause as `cycle_delay_range`** — a fix landed in this very subclause and did not sweep its neighbours. Every instance to date was found REACTIVELY, one construct at a time, by whatever the corpus tripped over. The actionable conclusion is not "more evidence for `LRM-GRAMMAR-FIDELITY`" but **an exhaustive Annex-A bracket/brace sweep**, which that tree should own.

**Fix (grammar-only, additive):** alternative 2 -> `kw_token_93ac8946 lbrack cycle_delay_const_range_expression rbrack -> {kind: "range", body: $3}`, using the existing `lbrack`/`rbrack` tokens `value_range_sv_2017` already uses for the same LRM construct. **Zero new rules or tokens — census 1477 UNCHANGED.** SV-only (`verilog_2005` byte-inert).

**Measured globally (guarded, both lanes):** repro matrix — all 4 bracketed forms REJECT->ACCEPT, **all 3 controls still ACCEPT** (`##[*]`/`##[+]` are reachable ONLY by backtracking PAST the edited alternative, so they were the real tripwire); AST LRM-faithful. Main `sv_2017` corpus 16,336: **pass 9,669 -> 9,692 (+23)**; adjudication **rejects-valid 406 -> 383 (-23, set-difference-verified ZERO new)**, **accepts-invalid 21 -> 21 BYTE-IDENTICAL**, match 5,703 -> 5,726. Targeting strictly surgical: the 23 flips are **exactly** the keyed `##[` rows, flipped-but-not-keyed = 0. **NO REGRESSION: 0 pass->fail AND 0 pass->timeout per-FILE.** `verilog_2005` lane BYTE-INERT (2,180/279, manifest `cmp`-identical). One `fail->timeout` row proven **jitter**, not regression: it contains zero `##` (the rule is never reached) and completes in 15 s with an unchanged `fail` verdict when run without 8-way contention.

**Gates (all GREEN, seeds 0/7/42), and notably BOTH contract JSONs untouched:** `sv_cert_recognized_union_gate` GREEN **with no re-baseline** (union_witness 1348 unchanged, residual `[]`, canonical UNKNOWN=11 / union 0, still `fully_certified_via_union`); `verilog_2005_conformance_gate` GREEN byte-inert (`1123/330/779/14`, matrix 240/0, orphans 0); `sv_syntax_closure_gate` 1,477 rules / 0 unreachable; `ast_shape_contract_gate` 18/0; `sv_external_corpus_triage_gate` PASS; `systemverilog_parser_book_gate` PASS; `sv_stimuli_quality_gate` PASS with `closed_loop_replay_targets_total` 126 -> 127 (+1 — the bracketed alternative is a NEW closed-loop generation target; feeds `SV-REPLAY-DEBT`, not a regression).

**Sibling surfaced and routed to a new leaf `.3.9` (NOT folded in):** 1 of the 24 keyed rows did not flip — it now parses PAST its old stuck point and dies at `## [*]`, a **spaced** star form. Alternatives 3/4 are **fused literal tokens** (`trivia "##[*]"`) that cannot admit the interior whitespace SystemVerilog's free-form lexing permits (`##[*]` ACCEPT / `## [*]` REJECT). Deferred deliberately: different mechanism, nothing regresses by deferring, and unlike this fix it renames **currently-produced** AST kinds (`{kind:"token_71b8cf7e"}` -> `{kind:"star"}`), so it is expected to bump the schema and deserves its own adjudication.

The second fix cut from the `.3.2`/v2 refreshed family map — after `.3.3` drained the #1 SVA family, **interface/modport (ch25), 50 rows** is the next single-construct family (verilator 24 / ispras 18 / sv-tests 3 / sv2v 3 / Surelog 1 / verible 1). **ROOT CAUSE (tool-pinned three ways + LRM-verified verbatim):** `grammars/systemverilog.ebnf:526` `modport_simple_ports_declaration := port_direction modport_simple_port` was **missing the LRM A.2.9 `{ , modport_simple_port }` repetition** — a single `port_direction` admitted only ONE port, so `modport master(input a, b, output c, d)` rejected at the shared-direction port `b` (`furthest_position=58`) while the control `modport master(input a, output c)` accepted; the scoped `--trace-rules` rule_stack showed the outer `modport_item ( comma modport_ports_declaration )*` unable to open a new group at `b`. IEEE 1800-2017 §25 / A.2.9 (verbatim, `docs/systemverilog/2017/md/section-25-interfaces.md:139`): `modport_simple_ports_declaration ::= port_direction modport_simple_port { , modport_simple_port }`. **FIX — TWO coupled grammar-only parts (hierarchy level 1):** (1) add the repetition — `modport_simple_ports_declaration := port_direction modport_simple_port ( comma modport_simple_port )*` with the family's proven `[$first, $rep::2*]` extraction-spread (`{direction, ports: [$2, $3::2*]}`; the emitted shape changes `port: $2` → the `ports` array — a schema `17`→`18` bump). (2) **⭐ a coupled `ref` reserved-word completion surfaced BY the measurement:** the modport-only regen first REGRESSED two previously-passing verilator files (`t_interface_virtual.v` / `t_interface_virtual_bad.v`, `modport phy(input addr, ref data)`) — tool-pinned to `ref` being a genuine SV `port_direction` (`port_direction_sv_only := kw_ref`) that was **erroneously omitted from `reserved_non_keyword_identifier_sv:402`** (which already lists `input`/`output`/`inout`), so the new greedy `( comma modport_simple_port )*` gobbled `ref` as a `port_identifier` (the engine's `*` does not backtrack across the rule boundary). Adding `ref` to the SV reserved list (IEEE 1800 Table B.1 reserves it; the `!reserved_non_keyword_identifier` negative guard) makes part 1 sound — with `ref` reserved, both `input a, b, output c, d` (stops at `output`) and `input addr, ref data` (stops at `ref`) parse. `verilog_2005` keeps its own list (`_v2005:405`, no `ref`), so v2005 is byte-inert. No new rule/token (census unchanged 1468). Same class as `SV-0036` (SV-reserved words that are legal `verilog_2005` identifiers). **MEASURED GLOBALLY (guarded re-characterization + adjudication):** repro matrix (control / shared-direction / modport-expr / `ref`-direction / the 2 formerly-regressed files) all ACCEPT under `sv_2017`, `verilog_2005` correctly REJECTS modport; AST carries the correct `{direction:{kind:"input"}, ports:[{...a},{...b}]}`. **Full external corpus 16,336: pass 9,433 → 9,459 (+26 net raw)** — 29 gains (verilator 13 / ispras 11 / Surelog 2 / sv2v 2 / opentitan 1) − 3 raw pass→fail (three `deferred:v2005_profile_lane` ivtest `.v` files declaring `reg ref;`: under `sv_2017` `ref` is now correctly reserved so they reject there — they stay v2005-lane-deferred and still ACCEPT under `verilog_2005`; consistent with how `logic`/`bit`-as-identifier Verilog files already reject under `sv_2017`); timeout 9 → 10 (one opentitan file at the 20 s boundary, already failing). **Adjudication (graduation) baseline: rejects-valid 481 → 454 (−27)** (verilator −13 / ispras −11 / sv2v −2 / Surelog −1), **accepts-invalid 21 → 21 (IDENTICAL set — no over-acceptance)**, **0 new rejects-valid** (`comm`-verified — no graduation regression), unexplained 502 → 475. **NO REGRESSION proof:** `verilog_2005_conformance_gate` GREEN byte-inert (lint orphans 0, corpus 240/0, cert deterministic seeds 0/7/42), `adjudication_manifest_v2005.tsv` BYTE-IDENTICAL + `results_v2005.tsv` sorted-identical; `systemverilog_parser_book_gate` GREEN; `sv_stimuli_quality_gate` + `sv_cert_recognized_union_gate` confirmed GREEN before commit. ## 2026-07-23 - PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0017 (leaf SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.2 DONE — read-only diagnosis) — 🗺️ the `.3` leaf-cutting map REFRESHED at the ADD-v1 vintage + a FOUNDATIONAL SVA finding: the `|->`/`|=>` implication operators are ABSENT from the grammar

Session #198. PNT pivots to the `.3` defect burn-down (the direct graduation blocker — 543 rejects-valid — chosen over `.9` coverage-authoring as the higher-value delivery work toward the NEXSIM SV `Done` bar). `.3.0`'s family map was built over the pre-ADD-v1 315-row population; this leaf refreshes the leaf-cutting map over the current 543-row population. **Two deterministic instruments:** (1) re-ran the tracked `stimuli/sv/cluster_rejects_valid.py` over the current manifest (543 rows, 247 stuck signatures; guarded 10 s / 152 MB peak) → `rejects_valid_clusters_v2.{tsv,md}` (the `.3.0` artifacts preserved unmodified); (2) NEW `stimuli/sv/classify_rejects_valid_families.py` — a priority-ordered structural bucketer over the stuck source line → `rejects_valid_families_v2.{tsv,md}` (byte-identical across two runs; `py_compile` clean). **The refreshed map: 543 rows → 13 construct families, ranked #1 SVA implication/property (ch16) 101 rows** (ispras 53 / verilator 31 / Surelog 8 / sv-tests 4), then interface/modport 50, constraint/randomize 23, compiler directives 22, spaced-based number literals 22, drive/charge strength 21, named-block/label 20, size/type cast 13, enum base range 9, foreach/array 9, unique0 6, coverage bins/cross 4, OTHER (per-row tail) 243. **⭐⭐ FOUNDATIONAL FINDING (tool-pinned WHY+WHERE, four independent confirmations):** the SV grammar is **missing the two core SVA sequence-implication operators `|->` (overlapped) and `|=>` (non-overlapped)** — no tokens, no `prop_primary` branches, and git `-S` proves they have NEVER been present. (1) A basic concurrent assertion `assert property (@(posedge clk) a |-> b)` is rejected (furthest at `|->`), while `assert property (@(posedge clk) p3)` with no implication PASSES — the gap is the operator, not the RHS. (2) The only `>`/`|` operator tokens are `implies` (`->`), `or_assign` (`|=`), `sequence_implies` (`=>`), `nonblocking_implies` (`->>`) — no `|->`, no `|=>`. (3) Scoped `--trace-rules prop_primary_sv_2017`: after the antecedent `sequence_expr` returns, no branch consumes `|->`. (4) IEEE 1800-2017 uses them pervasively (§17/§23 examples; `vpiOverlapImplyOp`/`vpiNonOverlapImplyOp` §83); the mangled `prop_primary` branches `implies property_expr`, `sequence_expr or_assign property_expr`, `property_expr implies property_expr` are the LRM-markdown→EBNF extractor's damaged remnants (it split the `|`-prefixed operators on `|` = the EBNF alternation metachar; the LRM-*extracted* grammar also lacks them). Reconciliation: H.12.5.8's "12/12" matrix tested only the WORD operators (until/or/and/intersect/within/##) — never `|->`/`|=>`, so this gap is orthogonal and open. **Impact:** explains the bulk of the 101-row SVA family and CONVERGES with `SV-REPLAY-DEBT`'s `prop_primary_*` cluster — one fix moves both SV `Done` axes. **VERIFIED (read-only, ADDRESSED + NO REGRESSION):** the refreshed 543-row family map over the whole population; determinism byte-proven (cluster re-run + classifier ×2); zero parser/grammar/generated/codegen surface touched (no release/schema/ledger moves); the `.3.0` artifacts preserved. **NEXT = `.3.3`:** add `|->`/`|=>` (tokens + `prop_primary_sv_2017`/`_sv_2023` branches, faithful to A.2.10, additive/low-risk) — regen + heavy battery + release/ledger/lockstep. ## 2026-07-23 - PGEN-BIN-BUILD-INTEGRITY-0007 (leaf BIN-BUILD-INTEGRITY.2 DONE, the tree's systemic fix) — 🔩 the standing gate that makes "a binary silently stops compiling" un-rottable: `make -C rust bin_build_integrity_gate`

Session #197. The tree's raison d'être: after three surfaces (`.1` a `required-features` binary, `.3` a maintained gate, `.5` a feature-gated integration test) were found rotted in the same blind spot — the batteries build `--lib`/`--tests` under DEFAULT features, a strict subset of what the repo ships — this leaf adds a maintained gate that closes the class. **New `rust/scripts/bin_build_integrity_gate.sh` + `make -C rust bin_build_integrity_gate`, doing two mechanical things: (1) a COVERAGE PROOF first — the binary census is derived from `cargo metadata --no-deps` (never a hand-list, so it cannot drift), and every declared binary's `required-features` must be satisfiable by ≥1 planned configuration (a new binary nobody planned for fails BY NAME, with the fix printed); (2) `cargo check --all-targets` per configuration — bins + lib + tests + benches + examples, so a feature-gated TEST module (`.5`'s class) is swept by the same pass as a `required-features` bin (`.1`'s class).** The plan is 5 configurations, each one the repo genuinely builds: `default` (feature `normal`), `bootstrap` (`--no-default-features --features bootstrap`), `generated_parsers` (the `focus_*` regen path), `ebnf_dual_run` (the `.ebnf` frontend), and `generated_parsers,ebnf_dual_run` (the documented dual-feature toolbox binary). **WHY a set of configurations, not one union build (decided, not defaulted): `--all-features` is INVALID here (`mimalloc_perf` and `never_free_arena_perf` both install a `#[global_allocator]`), and a union hides exactly the failure mode that rotted — code reachable only under ONE feature; `.5` proved this twice (a cfg-gated test runs 9/10 under one feature set and reports ok).** WHERE it does NOT go (the `.1` charter's guess, reversed on cost evidence): NOT folded into `ci_workflow_local_gate` — the dual configuration alone measured ~2 min and the feature sets share no build artifacts, so it is a standalone gate under the memory guard, the honest home for a heavy job. **VERIFIED: the gate exits 0 — coverage proof green (19 binaries, `uncovered_bins: []`, including the `.1` victim `ebnf_dual_run_diff`), all 5 configurations pass. ⭐ Earning the ADDRESSED box caught a real bug in the gate's own first draft: the dual config's features were space-separated in the plan string, which word-splits to `--features generated_parsers ebnf_dual_run` and makes cargo read the second feature as a stray positional (`error: unexpected argument 'ebnf_dual_run' found`) — the gate correctly reported that configuration as failing to compile; fixed by comma-joining (one argv token), re-run green. The gate flagging its own misconfiguration IS the proof it works.** NO REGRESSION: purely additive (script + `make` target + help line + book section); no Rust/grammar/generated/contract surface touched, so no parser, release, schema, or ledger moves; the coverage proof is a pure function of sorted `cargo metadata` and `cargo check` is deterministic on a fixed tree. Book lockstep: `docs/book/src/operations-and-governance.md` gains a "Build Integrity" section. Honest limit recorded in-tree: like every gate here, the un-bypassable leg is CI (E4), currently manual — re-enabling it as an auto CI job is the "no matter what" backstop, tracked as a future ops slice. **⭐ BIN-BUILD-INTEGRITY tree COMPLETE (all 5 leaves done): three rotted surfaces closed + a standing gate so the class cannot recur silently.**

## 2026-07-22 - PGEN-BIN-BUILD-INTEGRITY-0006 (leaf BIN-BUILD-INTEGRITY.5 DONE) — ⚠️ a THIRD silently-rotted surface: the 10-grammar return-annotation shape integration test has not compiled since 2026-07-12, and the `.2` gate found it before it even landed

Session #197. While measuring the cost of the `.2` build-integrity gate, its very first configuration check failed: `cargo check --all-targets --features "generated_parsers ebnf_dual_run"` → `error: could not compile pgen (test "auto_return_annotation_shape_gate_integration") due to 10 previous errors`. **This ANSWERS the open question `.2`'s charter had recorded** ("whether the same hole exists for `#[cfg(feature = ...)]` TEST modules") — **yes, with a measured instance.** `rust/tests/auto_return_annotation_shape_gate_integration.rs` carries `#![cfg(feature = "generated_parsers")]` (`:26`), so plain `cargo test` (default features) compiles it to an empty crate, while every battery that DOES enable `generated_parsers` builds `--lib` and never `--tests`: the intersection is empty, and nothing in the repository compiles this file. **ROOT CAUSE (WHY + WHERE):** commit `961b1781` (2026-07-12, `PGEN-RGX-0078-0031`, the node-arena landing worth −21.9% on regex) added a second constructor parameter to every generated parser — `pub fn new(input: &'input str, arena: &'input NodeArena<'input>, logger: Box<dyn Logger>)` (`generated/regex_parser.rs:1065`). In-tree callers were migrated to the house idiom (`parser_registry.rs:522`+), but this file — last touched 2026-04-27 — was not: **10 × `error[E0061]: this function takes 3 arguments but 2 arguments were supplied`, "argument #2 of type `&NodeArena<'_>` is missing"**, at `:86`/`:121`/`:149`/`:173`/`:194`/`:222`/`:241`/`:261`/`:290`/`:318` — one per grammar the gate covers (regex, return_annotation, semantic_annotation, rtl_const_expr, rtl_frontend, json, vhdl, systemverilog_preprocessor, systemverilog, ebnf). **FIX (same narrowest level as `.1`): the house idiom at each site** — `let node_arena = pgen::ast_pipeline::NodeArena::new();` constructed inside each parse closure, then `&node_arena` as argument 2. No test logic, sample, assertion, or logger channel changed. **VERIFIED before → after, and run TWICE because the tenth test needs a second feature: under `--features generated_parsers`, 9 passed / 0 failed (the `auto_gate_ebnf_*` case is additionally `#[cfg(feature = "ebnf_dual_run")]`, so it is correctly excluded); under `--features "generated_parsers ebnf_dual_run"`, 10 passed / 0 failed — every repaired call site EXECUTED against real generated parsers, not merely compiled.** That tenth site is itself a second independent argument for checking CONFIGURATIONS rather than one union build. `clippy_on_rust_change` source-strict PASS (generated-stage debt unchanged at 291). No library, grammar, generated, or contract surface touched — no parser, release, schema, or ledger moved. Three rotted surfaces have now been found in this one blind spot (a `required-features` binary, a maintained gate, and a feature-gated integration test), which is the case for landing `.2` next.

## 2026-07-22 - PGEN-BIN-BUILD-INTEGRITY-0005 (leaf BIN-BUILD-INTEGRITY.3 DONE, script-only) — 🟢 `ebnf_frontend_dual_run_gate` is GREEN again after 7 days RED; the design call is adjudicated on a byte-identity measurement, and a recurring trap dies with it

Session #197. **ROOT CAUSE (WHY + WHERE):** the gate built its `ast_pipeline` with `--features ebnf_dual_run` ONLY, then asked that binary to `--generate-parser` from the annotation-bearing `grammars/ebnf.ebnf` (`ebnf_frontend_dual_run_diff_gate.sh:92`); commit `200cae5b` (2026-07-15) made exactly that combination a hard refusal at `rust/src/ast_pipeline/mod.rs:3925` (`require_bootstrap_annotation_fallback_license`), and the gate script — untouched since 2026-04-06 — never learned about it. **THE DESIGN CALL THIS LEAF OWNED, ADJUDICATED ON MEASUREMENT: (a) build with `generated_parsers` too**, not (b) opt into `PGEN_ALLOW_BOOTSTRAP_ANNOTATION_FALLBACK=1` (which the leaf's charter had tentatively favored). First the measurement that removes "which output is right?" from the question: the same Perl-frontend JSON generated through the canonical backend and through the opted-in fallback yields a **BYTE-IDENTICAL parser** (sha256 `56cf0763c13bbbd4bfe3c02a52fe3fb9e342a3650bcb61307afbf6d13e3638c0`, 12,445,288 B, written to the SAME output path both times so the ~3k path-embedded diagnostic strings are controlled) — so (a) costs nothing measurable today, and the choice is purely about what is sound to depend on tomorrow. Four grounds: **(1)** a differential must vary exactly ONE thing (Perl frontend vs Rust frontend) — a degradable annotation backend on the Rust arm is a second, uncontrolled variable, and a future divergence could not be attributed; **(2)** the fallback's own license covers only artifacts "re-derived canonically and [passing] `parse_harness_equivalence_gate` before being trusted", which a standing gate cannot satisfy per run; **(3)** it restores the `200cae5b` decision record's stated invariant ("the `ebnf_dual_run`-only frontend binary performs only standalone raw-AST export (no annotation parsing)") — false for exactly this ONE call site — instead of carving a permanent exception into it; **(4) ⭐** `TOOLBOX.md` defines `rust/target/debug/ast_pipeline` as the DUAL-feature binary, so the gate was overwriting the shared toolbox binary with a single-feature build — the trap `MEMORY.md` records being re-hit as recently as `-0015`; verified gone (the binary reports `ebnf_dual_run=true generated_parsers=true` after the run). Not a cold-clone hazard: `rust/build.rs` presence-gates every generated-parser include behind its own `has_generated_*` cfg. Scope minimal — only the `ast_pipeline` build line changes; `ebnf_dual_run_diff` stays single-feature deliberately (it only PARSES grammar files and never calls annotation extraction, so it cannot reach the refusal). **VERIFIED before → after: before, exit 1 at the bootstrap step with no grammar ever compared; after, exit 0 in STRICT mode with all three tracked grammars passing — `ebnf` 131/131 raw_ast parity (23787/23788 B, 100.00%), `json` 19/19 parity (99.90%), `regex` full parse parity (157306/157306, 100.00%) — which REPRODUCES the last known-green 2026-06-25 baseline exactly, i.e. the gate was restored, not redefined. ## 2026-07-22 - PGEN-BIN-BUILD-INTEGRITY-0004 (leaf BIN-BUILD-INTEGRITY.4 DONE, script-only) — the gate's own failure diagnostics have been DEAD since the day they were added: a `set -e` abort made the excerpt printer unreachable

Session #197. Found while reproducing `.3` (the RED `ebnf_frontend_dual_run_gate`): the gate failed with **no cause on screen** — just `==> Regenerating EBNF frontend artifacts for dual-run harness` followed by `make: *** [ebnf_frontend_dual_run_gate] Error 1`, while the real error sat unread in `logs/bootstrap_generate_ebnf_parser.log`. That is exactly the symptom the **2026-04-06 CI-observability fix** was written to cure (its tracker note in `LIVE_ACHIEVEMENT_STATUS.md` states the script "now prints the hidden log path and bounded head/tail excerpts whenever either bootstrap step fails"). **ROOT CAUSE (WHY + WHERE):** `rust/scripts/ebnf_frontend_dual_run_diff_gate.sh` runs under `set -euo pipefail` (`:2`), and its helper `run_logged_or_dump` (`:61`) invoked the work UNGUARDED — `"$@" >"$log_path" 2>&1` then `local status=$?` (`:66`–`:67`). Under `errexit`, a failing command inside a function whose call is not in a tested context aborts the shell **at that command**, so the status capture, `print_log_excerpt_on_failure`, and `return "$status"` are all unreachable: the entire diagnostic block is dead code, and has been since it was added. Pinned two ways — the live RED gate printing nothing, plus a minimal isolating bash probe of the same shape (`set -euo pipefail` + the same helper + `false`) which exits 1 without ever printing its marker line. **FIX (narrowest level that works, script-only): `local status=0; "$@" >"$log_path" 2>&1 || status=$?`** — `|| status=$?` keeps errexit from firing at that command; everything else is untouched, and the helper still RETURNS the real exit code so the caller still fails fast at the same step. **VERIFIED before → after on the same still-RED gate, same exit code 1: before, zero diagnostic output; after, the run prints `error: bootstrap EBNF parser generation failed with exit code 1`, the `log:` path, and the full excerpt carrying the verbatim `Error: REFUSED: return annotation '{type: "grammar_file", elements: [$1*]}' needs the generated annotation backend …` line** — the failure is self-explaining for the first time since the capability was claimed. **SIBLING CENSUS (this is a lone defect, not a class):** all 13 other `<var>=$?` capture sites across the gate surface are correctly guarded — `set +e`/`set -e` brackets, `if/else` arms, EXIT-trap handlers where `$?` is the trap's own status, an explicit `|| rc=$?`, or a script that does not set `errexit`; 0 further defects found. No Rust/grammar/generated surface touched, so no parser, gate verdict, or artifact can move; `.3` (the refusal itself) remains open and is the next slice.

## 2026-07-21 - PGEN-RGX-0089-0001 (tree RGX-0089) — REJECTS-VALID REGRESSION FIXED: `\b` inside the extended class `(?[...])` accepts again (release 1.1.106 / contract 1.1.109 / ledger REGEX-0115); all three director-directed RGX adoption blockers now addressed

Session #188, third of the three director-directed RGX adoption-blocker reports (0091 ✓ → 0090 ✓ → **0089** ✓).

**The regression (downstream `PGEN-RGX-0089`; present `1.1.82`→`1.1.105`).** PGEN rejected `(?[\b])`, `(?[[\b]])`, and the shipped RGX fixture `(?[\a | \b | \e | \f])+` — PCRE2 10.47 accepts all and matches U+0008. Root cause trace-proven: release `1.1.82` (`.3.13`, commit `40202cb0`, pinned by `git log -S`) dropped the escape-anchor letters from `simple_escape`'s positive set — sound at body level where `anchor` owns `\b` (and `\b*` correctly rejects err 109), but `extended_class_element` routes escapes through the generic `escape` rule where `anchor` is unreachable, so `\b` lost its ONLY extended-class derivation (`--trace-rules`: `escape_unit` exhausts all branches at position 4). Ordinary `[\b]` was unaffected (`class_simple_escape` keeps `b`). Undetected for ~23 releases: grammar-derived stimuli cannot emit a derivation the grammar lacks (the rejects-valid blind spot — director observation recorded, action deferred) and the conformance corpus has no `(?[\b])` cell.

**The fix (grammar tier).** A dedicated positive branch `extended_class_backspace_escape = "\\b" -> {type: "escape", kind: "shorthand", char: "b"}` on `extended_class_element` — the grammar encoding of PCRE2's class-context dual meaning, extended classes only (body-level `\b` stays an anchor; NOT re-added to `simple_escape`, which would regress `.3.13`).
