## 2026-07-11 - PGEN-FPP-0004 — FINAL-PHASE-PREDICATE.3: close the multi-branch `view` footgun via an other-view resolver FALLBACK (tier-5 engine robustness, INERT on every shipped parser)

Engine-robustness slice completing the `FINAL-PHASE-PREDICATE` tree (all three children now landed). No release/contract/schema/ledger bump — the change is byte-identical on every shipped parser. Closes the footgun the FIRST consumer (`REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY.4.11`) surfaced and retires the per-consumer `view: shaped` workaround it had to use.

**The footgun.** A `@predicate` defaults to `view: raw`. On a MULTI-BRANCH (`Or`) rule the winning branch captures its raw `Sequence` as the final-predicate view, so a shaped-key `$ref`/`$name` (naming a `-> {…}` transform field) cannot resolve against the `Sequence` — the rule raises *"could not resolve attribute reference 'ref'"* and REJECTS even a DEFINED name. A single-branch rule resolved the same key only by the `semantic_raw_content == None` shaped-fallback ACCIDENT, which is why the `.2` single-branch isolation proof missed it. Root-caused tools-first in session #87 via `--trace-rules`.

**The fix (Option (b)-refined, director-authorized — a resolver fallback, NOT a default-flip).** Each argument resolver now computes `(selected_content, fallback_content)` from `spec.view` (the OTHER view is the fallback); a NAMED / object-key reference absent from the primary view falls back to the other content view BEFORE raising the unresolved-attribute error. Gated by a new shared `semantic_reference_is_named` helper mirroring `resolve_semantic_reference`'s named-vs-positional split — a positional `$N` walks the raw tree structurally and is NEVER retried against the other view (positional `$N` / `$text` semantics unchanged), and a key absent from BOTH views still errors (a real typo is never masked). Applies to ALL phases (pre/branch/post/final). Landed identically in the codegen-emitted resolver (`ast_based_generator.rs` `resolve_semantic_predicate_spec_against_content` + `try_…`, threaded through the value/try/properties resolvers) and its interpreter mirror (`parse_harness_interpreter.rs`). `@emit_fact` (an effect, not a predicate) passes its own single content as the inert fallback (byte-identical). `semantic_runtime.rs:3572` (`evaluate_content_aware_predicate`) needed NO change — it consumes `selected_content` only for `content_kind_is` (a content-KIND query, not a `$ref` resolution). Fix-hierarchy tier-5 (engine): the footgun is an engine-resolution inconsistency, not fixable below the engine except by the per-consumer `view: shaped` workaround this leaf retires.

**Proven (all re-runnable oracles, on the regenerated 11-parser set).** Scratch-slot isolation in a REAL generated parser: multi-branch default-view `has_fact(name_decl, $r) phase: final` → `k<a>decl a;` / `g<a>decl a;` (both branches) forward-ACCEPT, `k<a>decl b;` REJECT (obligation args resolved to `Identifier("a")` VIA the fallback). `parse_harness_semantic_gate` **36/36 CLEAN** — new MULTI-BRANCH default-view case `sem_final_multibranch_shaped_ref` byte-identical (interpreter == compile-and-run oracle) + 3 anchors; the 35 prior cases unchanged. `parse_harness_equivalence_gate` `certified_grammars_are_byte_identical` over all **11** shipped parsers **regenerated with the new codegen** (INERT-ON-SHIPPED — regex's `.4.11` gates keep explicit `view: shaped`, resolve in-primary, never touch the fallback). `parse_harness_combinator_gate` 27/27. `duality_hunt_gate` pinned signatures unchanged. `regex_ast_shape_contract_gate` aligned=4 drift=0. Regex cert `--entry-rule regex --count 40` seeds 0/7/42 **UNKNOWN=0 fully_certified=true** (witness 258, spf 0/1/1 — byte-identical to the `.4.11` baseline). Named-ref spot-check `\k<aa>(?'aa'x)` / `(?&a)(?<a>x)` ACCEPT + `\k<zzz>` REJECT intact. Stage-1 source clippy exit 0. LOCKSTEP: book `semantic-store.md` (`view` note softened from "REQUIRED" to "optional self-documentation") + `parse-harness.md` (new row + 35→36) + `TOOLBOX.md` §1.8 (35→36) + decision record `.3 BUILD LANDED` anchor + tree + this file + `DEVELOPMENT_NOTES.md` + `LIVE_ACHIEVEMENT_STATUS.md` + `MEMORY.md`.

## 2026-07-11 - PGEN-REGEX-PCRE2-0045 — REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY.4.11: named-reference UNKNOWN-name reject is now GRAMMAR-owned (a genuine accepts-invalid correction — behavior-CHANGING; FIRST consumer of the `phase: final` primitive)

Regex release `1.1.102`→`1.1.103`, contract `1.1.104`→`1.1.105`, AST-dump schema `1`, ledger `REGEX-0098` Deferred→Fixed. A named reference to a group name defined NOWHERE in the pattern now **REJECTS** (PCRE2 err 115 "reference to non-existent subpattern") while a **legal forward reference** still **ACCEPTs** — closing a real released-parser accepts-invalid gap. All nine unknown-name spellings flip ACCEPT→REJECT: `\k<zzz>` / `\k'zzz'` / `\k{zzz}` (named backreferences), `(?P=zzz)` (Python), `\g{zzz}` (braced), `(?&zzz)` / `(?P>zzz)` / `\g<zzz>` / `\g'zzz'` (named subroutine calls); the controls `(?'aa'x)\k<aa>`, `\k<aa>(?'aa'x)` (forward), `(?<a>x)(?&a)`, `(?&a)(?<a>x)` (forward subroutine), `\g{a}(?<a>x)`, and every NUMERIC form (`(a)\1`, `(a)(b)\g<2>`, `(a)(?1)`) stay ACCEPT. Frozen acceptance spec = the `.3.22` oracle matrix, **17/17**.

**The FIRST consumer of the `FINAL-PHASE-PREDICATE` primitive.** Encoded purely in `grammars/regex.ebnf` (no engine/Rust logic change — only the release-version constants): (1) a two-kind fact split — `regex_defined_capture_name` (parse INVENTORY, `@emit_fact name=$name` on the shaped `named_group`/`python_named_group` rules) vs `regex_capture_name` (gen-draw SOURCE, `@gen_emit_fact` on the bare `capture_name`) — so the stimuli generator (which keys fact-draws on the producer rule's WHOLE RENDER) never splices a whole `(?<name>…)` group into a reference slot; (2) named forms peeled into HOMOGENEOUS rules so the whole-input gate binds to every named branch and never the numeric siblings — `named_backreference` (6 br), `named_subroutine_target` (2 br), a shared `reference_name` carrier, `braced_name_ref` removed; (3) `has_fact(regex_defined_capture_name, $ref|$name) phase: final, view: shaped` on the three named-reference gates.

**Root cause of the multi-branch bug (proven tools-first, `--trace-rules`).** The first build rejected even DEFINED names: a `@predicate` defaults to `view: raw`, and a multi-branch tournament captures the winner's raw `Sequence` for the final-predicate view — so a shaped-key `$ref` cannot resolve ("could not resolve attribute reference 'ref'") and the rule rejects. Single-branch rules only worked by the `semantic_raw_content=None` shaped-fallback accident (why the FPP.2 single-branch isolation proof missed it). Fix = `view: shaped` (fix-hierarchy level 1). A second bug (`\g<zzz>` accepting undefined) SELF-RESOLVED: once `named_backreference` no longer fails structurally, longest-match routes `\g<zzz>` to it over `simple_escape` — no `!"g"` guard needed. See `docs/decisions/project_final_phase_deferred_predicate_primitive.md` (FIRST-CONSUMER FINDING) + the book `phase: final` section (now documents the multi-branch `view: shaped` requirement).

**Conformance:** `.3.22` oracle matrix **17/17**; regex cert-coverage seeds 0/7/42 **UNKNOWN 2→0, `fully_certified=true`** (witness 256→258 — the named-ref rules are witnessable again); spf independence proven by a decisive clean-main baseline (clean-main **2/2/0** vs `.4.11` **0/1/1** — a NET improvement, so the residual pre-existing `\Q\E`/conditional generator spf is NOT a regression); `ast_shape_contract` regex **aligned=4 drift=0** (inventory 236→238 re-synced; accepted-AST byte-identical — `view` is a predicate, not a return-shape); `certified_grammars_are_byte_identical` regex byte-identical (the interpreter mirror honors `view: shaped`); `duality_hunt_gate` pass; `regex_pcre2_compile_oracle_gate` recorded in ledger `REGEX-0098`. Downstream (RGX): PGEN now rejects unknown-name named references — the `1.1.x` closure the prior contract notes promised.

## 2026-07-10 - PGEN-FPP-0002 — FINAL-PHASE-PREDICATE.2: the `phase: final` whole-input deferred-obligation predicate — ENGINE PRIMITIVE BUILT (shared core + codegen + interpreter mirror + gated), proven in isolation before any consumer

Tier-5 engine slice implementing the frozen BUILD SPEC from `PGEN-FPP-0001`. A GENERAL, parser-agnostic fourth `@predicate` phase — **`phase: final`** — that validates a **legal forward reference** (a reference whose definition may appear LATER in the input), which `pre`/`branch`/`post` provably cannot express. No release/contract/schema/ledger bump: the primitive is INERT on every shipped parser (no grammar uses it yet), so no released-parser behavior changed. The shared unlock for `REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY.4.11` (named-ref UNKNOWN-name — the real accepts-invalid fix, ledger `REGEX-0098`) + `.4.7` (scan-substring capture inventory), which are leaves of the regex tree whose frontier now passes.

**What `phase: final` is.** Not an inline gate on its own rule (the rule has already committed). At rule commit it resolves its args against the carrying rule's captured content (so `$name` becomes the concrete captured string) and enqueues a **deferred obligation** `(predicate, resolved_args, source_position)`; the obligation rides speculation rollback exactly like `@emit_fact` (a losing/failed branch's obligation never survives). At top-level `parse_full` success — when the whole input is consumed and the store holds the complete inventory — a terminal discharge pass evaluates every obligation in ascending source-position order through the existing `evaluate_predicate`; the first `Some(false)` fails the whole parse at its position (validator first-error-by-position). It composes with the entire predicate vocabulary (`has_fact`, `fact_count_at_least`, …) — `final` is the *when*, the whole-input generalization of `post`. Backpatching generalized to a semantic check (LLVM `ForwardRefVals`→`validateEndOfModule`; Dragon §6.7).

**How (mirrored + gated, per the frozen spec).** Shared core `rust/src/ast_pipeline/semantic_runtime.rs`: `SemanticPredicatePhase::Final` (+ `parse` aliases `final`/`parse_complete`/`whole_input`, widened reject message), `is_final_predicate()`, accessors `final_predicates_for_rule`/`has_final_predicates_for_rule`/`needs_raw_final_capture_for_rule`, `DeferredObligation{spec,source_position}`, `SemanticRuntimeState.deferred_obligations`, `SemanticRuntimeCheckpoint.deferred_len` (recorded in `checkpoint()`, truncated in `rollback_to_named`), `SemanticRuntimeDelta.new_obligations` (captured in `extract_delta_since`, replayed in `apply_delta`, folded into `is_empty`), `enqueue_deferred_obligation` + `discharge_deferred_obligations`. Obligations NEVER bump `write_epoch` (inert until discharge ⇒ cannot taint the memo). Codegen `ast_based_generator.rs` (emitted into every generated parser): a `discharge_final_phase_obligations` helper called in `parse_full` AND `parse_full_from` after full-consume (Err → `ParseError::ContextualError`); a post-body enqueue loop (resolve args like a post predicate, then `enqueue_deferred_obligation(resolved_spec, node.span.start)`), placed after the post-gate block so a post-rejected rule never enqueues; the raw-capture gate OR-in of `needs_raw_final_capture_for_rule`; the phase serializer `Final` arm. Interpreter mirror `parse_harness_interpreter.rs`: the identical enqueue loop + raw-capture OR-in + discharge at top-level completion (Err → an `accepted:false` `ParseOutcome`).

**Duality-clean (no `.4.8`-style break).** `phase: final` gates no branch during the single pass, so the stimuli generator ignores it (catch-all); each consumer keeps its existing conservative `@gen_predicate` draw (references only already-emitted names ⇒ never emits an invalid forward ref). NO new generation primitive — the `lacks_fact`-branch-prune trap that killed `.4.8`'s A′ does not recur.

**Proven in isolation before any consumer (the RSVC/SCP model).** Scratch-slot generated parser: forward reference `use a;decl a;` → ACCEPT (rc 0); undefined `use a;decl b;` → REJECT (rc 1, `whole-input predicate 'has_fact' not satisfied at parse completion`, `furthest_position=11`) — a `post` gate could NOT accept the forward case. The `.6.2` semantic gate gains two constructs — `FinalForwardGate` (`sem_final_forward_gate`) + `FinalRollbackSpeculation` (`sem_final_rollback_speculation`, a losing longest-match branch's obligation discarded vs the winner's discharging) — both **CLEAN** (interpreter byte-identical to the compile-and-run oracle + independent anchors hold).

**Verification.** `parse_harness_semantic_gate` **35/35 CLEAN** (`2 passed; 0 failed`) — the 33 pre-existing cases stay `diverge=0` ⇒ codegen+interpreter changes byte-neutral. `parse_harness_equivalence_gate` **4/4 pass** — the 11 shipped/certified grammars byte-identical (inert on shipped). `parse_harness_combinator_gate` 27/27 structural intact. `cargo check`/clippy clean. LOCKSTEP: `docs/book/src/semantic-store.md` (the `final` phase + forward-reference subsection) + `docs/book/src/parse-harness.md` (2 construct rows + case count) + `TOOLBOX.md` §1.8 + decision record `BUILD LANDED` anchors + tree `docs/tasks/FINAL-PHASE-PREDICATE.md` (`.2` done + acceptance checklist) + MEMORY resume pointer. Next: the regex consumers (`.4.11` then `.4.7`) in the REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY tree.

## 2026-07-10 - PGEN-FPP-0001 — FINAL-PHASE-PREDICATE.1: the `phase: final` whole-input predicate primitive — SOTA-cited A-vs-B DESIGN DECIDED (Option B) + frozen engine BUILD SPEC (PURE-DOCS, no code change)

Design slice for a GENERAL, parser-agnostic engine primitive — no release/contract/schema bump, no grammar/Rust/codegen/generated change. Executes the director-authorized (2026-07-10, *"do what you see fit to achieve sota, signoff level quality"*) SOTA-cited DESIGN slice that the endorsement required BEFORE any engine code. The shared unlock for `REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY.4.11` (named-reference UNKNOWN-name — the real accepts-invalid fix, ledger `REGEX-0098`) and `.4.7` (scan-substring capture inventory). Direct sibling of the `RULE-SPAN-VALUE-CONSTRAINT` / `SCOPE-CONTEXT-PREDICATE` primitives.

**The gap.** A grammar cannot validate a **legal forward reference** — a reference whose definition appears LATER in the input than the reference (regex `\k<name>` named backrefs, `(*scs:(N))` scan-substring lists, subroutine calls; also declaration-order-free symbol use). Tool-verified this session: the `@predicate` phase enum is exactly `Pre | Branch | Post` (`semantic_runtime.rs:1001-1007`), all per-rule and left-to-right; every fact-producing effect fires post-body (`ast_based_generator.rs:2100-2109`, branch-start `:3872-3890`); there is NO on-enter emit and NO whole-input/terminal phase anywhere (engine-wide grep: zero hits). So a `has_fact`/`post` gate on a reference fires BEFORE a later definition is emitted and would REJECT the legal forward reference. This is the attribute-grammar impossibility, not a coding gap: a forward reference is a non-L-attributed (right-to-left) dependency ⇒ provably not single-left-to-right-evaluable (Dragon §5.2.3–5.2.4; Knuth 1968; Bochmann 1976). The only status-quo alternative is an out-of-band host validator (`validate_regex_compile_contract` at `parser_registry.rs:1223`), which is invisible to the stimuli generator — the EBNF-single-source-of-truth defect the whole `.4` family is deleting.

**The primitive (chosen).** A fourth `@predicate` phase, **`phase: final`**: checked ONCE at whole-input parse completion (`parse_full` success, `ast_based_generator.rs:1649-1663`) against the now-complete semantic store — so it sees facts emitted ANYWHERE, including LATER than the carrying rule. Realized via **deferred obligations**: a `final` predicate resolves its args against the rule's captures at rule-commit, enqueues a transactional obligation `(predicate, resolved_args, position)` (rides speculation rollback like `@emit_fact`), and a terminal discharge pass evaluates them all — in ascending source-position order, through the existing `evaluate_predicate` — at parse completion; the first `Some(false)` fails the parse with its position. It composes with the whole existing predicate vocabulary (`has_fact` set-membership, `fact_count_at_least` whole-input count, `value_compare`, …): `final` is the *when*, the whole-input generalization of `post`.

**A-vs-B → B (single pass + deferred obligations), not A (two-pass pre-scan).** The SOTA survey's discriminator (primary sources): a pre-pass (PCRE2 `parse_regex`; .NET `CountCaptures`→`ScanRegex`) is warranted ONLY when an *irreversible pre-emission global aggregate* forces the count to be known before the main pass (PCRE2 memory-sizing/opcode selection — `HACKING`: "full knowledge of group names and numbers throughout"). A reference *validator* has no such dependency, so it defers — the LLVM `LLParser` `ForwardRefVals`→`validateEndOfModule` / Dragon §6.7 backpatching / Rust-Roslyn late-binding pattern. B reuses PGEN's one authoritative parse + the store that already survives to a clean whole-pattern state at completion (facts are global, never retracted on `@close_scope`), so the terminal check cannot diverge from the parse; A would force re-running the grammar's structural recognition (the price PCRE2 pays with a separate hand-written scanner). B is one general parser-agnostic primitive; A is per-consumer bespoke. Fix-hierarchy tier-5 (engine), proven necessary (the phase enumeration is the proof nothing lower can see a forward capture).

**Duality-clean (no `.4.8`-style break).** `phase: final` gates no branch during the single pass, so the stimuli generator ignores it safely (catch-all `stimuli_generator.rs:7759`); each consumer keeps its existing conservative `@gen_predicate` draw (references only already-emitted names ⇒ sound, never emits an invalid forward ref). NO new generation primitive — the `lacks_fact`-branch-prune trap that killed `.4.8`'s fact-based A′ does not recur.

**Deliverables (PURE-DOCS).** Decision record `docs/decisions/project_final_phase_deferred_predicate_primitive.md` (SOTA survey + A-vs-B table + discriminator + frozen engine BUILD SPEC + consumer mapping) + INDEX row; new tree `docs/tasks/FINAL-PHASE-PREDICATE.md` (`.1` DESIGN done `PGEN-FPP-0001`, `.2` BUILD pending) + `TASK_TREE.md` row; `REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY.md` A-vs-B DECISION section + `.4.7`/`.4.11` leaf cross-refs; MEMORY resume pointer. NO engine/grammar/codegen/generated/manifest/book change (no user-visible behavior yet — the book updates when `.2` builds the primitive). Next slice = `FINAL-PHASE-PREDICATE.2` (engine BUILD, mirrored + parse-harness-gated, proven in isolation before any consumer).

## 2026-07-10 - PGEN-REGEX-PCRE2-0044 — REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY.4.8: the PCRE2 start-option POSITION rule is now GRAMMAR-owned (behavior-NEUTRAL validator→grammar migration + standalone validator-check DELETION), enforced PURELY STRUCTURALLY

Released regex slice — release `1.1.101`→`1.1.102`, contract `1.1.103`→`1.1.104`, AST-dump schema stays `1`, ledger `REGEX-0112`.

**What / why.** A PCRE2 start option (`(*UTF)`, `(*CRLF)`, `(*LIMIT_HEAP=…)`, …) is valid ONLY as a contiguous run at the very start of the WHOLE pattern — never after any construct, never in a later alternative, never nested at any depth (`pcre2test` 10.47: `(*CRLF)abc` ACCEPT; `a(*CR)b`, `(a)(*CRLF)`, `((*CRLF)a)`, `(?:(*CRLF)a)`, `(?=(*CRLF)a)`, `(*CRLF)a|(*LF)b`, `a(*CRLF)|b` all err 160). The released parser already REJECTED all of these, but via the out-of-band validator `find_invalid_verb_construct` + `is_start_option_position`, while the GRAMMAR alone ACCEPTED them (a start option was an ungated `directive_verb_nonquant` piece valid in any position) — a single-source-of-truth hole. **Behavior-NEUTRAL migration**: the released `--parse` verdict is byte-identical (the released `--parse` 27-case oracle matrix — 13 accept + 14 reject — matches `pcre2test` exactly); the reject moves validator→grammar and both validator functions are DELETED.

**How (PURELY STRUCTURAL — grammar design A″, no fact/predicate, no engine change).** `regex` now enters through a distinguished `entry_alternation` chain (`entry_alternation = entry_alternative ("|" alternative)*`; `entry_alternative = entry_concatenation?`; `entry_concatenation = start_option_piece+ piece* -> [$1*, $2**] | piece+ -> [$1**]`) that mirrors the shared `alternation`/`alternative`/`concatenation` byte-for-byte, except that `entry_concatenation`'s first branch admits a leading `start_option_piece+` run. `start_option_piece` (peeled out of `directive_verb_nonquant`) is referenced ONLY from `entry_concatenation`; every later `|`-alternative and every nested pattern uses the shared `alternative`/`concatenation`, which have no start-option branch — so a mis-positioned start option simply has NO derivation and fails to parse. The validator `find_invalid_verb_construct` + `is_start_option_position` were DELETED (4 helpers stay — still used by the lookbehind-length walk). Because the rule is structural, it costs NOTHING on the parse hot path (the fastest option, aligning with the RGX-0078 speed priority) and the stimuli generator cannot emit a mis-positioned start option either — the generator↔parser duality is closed BY CONSTRUCTION.

**A′→A″ pivot (recorded for transparency — the director had chosen the fact-based A′).** A′ was built first exactly per the frozen spec (an epsilon `body_boundary` emitting a monotonic `regex_body_started` fact + a `@predicate lacks_fact` gate) and PARSE-derisked green via the certified interpreter (byte-identical + full oracle). But the cert then surfaced a generation defect: the stimuli generator's store-aware machinery has NO `lacks_fact` branch-prune (only `fact_count_at_least` count-prune + `has_fact` name-draw), so `@gen_predicate lacks_fact` could not stop the generator from emitting mis-positioned start options — which the A′ grammar then rejected (cert `sample_parse_failures` 0→65, a duality break). Making A′ generation-clean would need a NEW gen-engine primitive; per the fix hierarchy (grammar before engine), A″ (structural) is the clean grammar-only fix that resolves it with no engine change, no fact, and no gen-side steering. A″ re-derisked green on the same suite.

**Verification (all seeds 0/7/42).** Grammar-only migration test `rust/tests/regex_start_option_position_grammar_migration.rs` GREEN (14 mis-positioned forms REJECT + controls ACCEPT, oracle-verified); released `--parse` 27-case oracle matrix all matching `pcre2test` 10.47. regex cert `265/265 UNKNOWN=0 fully_certified=true` (259→265: +6 rules); `--lint-grammar` 0 errors (265 rules); `duality_hunt_gate` 6 regex lanes REBASELINED (the start-option-prefix break VANISHED — A″ closed the class; the hunter re-targeted a PRE-EXISTING generic "did not consume full input" generator over-approximation — quantifier-on-comment `(?#)?+`, unbalanced parens, conditionals — that PCRE2 ALSO rejects and the parser correctly rejects; pinned + tracked as `.4.8.1`, NOT a `.4.8` regression: verdict+furthest-pos identical on the pre-`.4.8` grammar); `parse_harness_equivalence_gate` regex byte-identical; `ast_shape_contract` regex aligned (inventory 232→236); `regex_pcre2_compile_oracle_gate` bounds SATISFIED — A″ `2189/1871/270/48` (match ≥ 1845, false-accept ≤ 299, false-reject 48 at the ceiling ⇒ zero new false-rejects), **byte-identical to pristine** (a grammar-verdict flip-diff over all 283 corpus `(*` patterns finds EXACTLY ONE change, `a(*CR)b`, which the released validator already rejected → released-neutral; the prior pristine-HEAD gate summary is likewise `2189/1871/270/48`). ⚠️ the `2189/1867/274/48` tuple quoted in earlier release entries is STALE (a pre-existing `fa` 274→270 doc-drift, not a `.4.8` change; the gate asserts bounds, which masked it). 36 remaining `regex_compile_validation` unit tests green; `metadata_is_stable` at `1.1.102`/`1.1.104`. cert `sample_parse_failures` 4/4/6 = the same tracked over-approximation (`.4.8.1`), not a start-option issue.

## 2026-07-10 - PGEN-REGEX-PCRE2-0038 — REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY.4.10: `\K`-in-lookaround is now GRAMMAR-owned (behavior-NEUTRAL validator→grammar migration + standalone validator-check DELETION)

Released regex slice — release `1.1.100`→`1.1.101`, contract `1.1.102`→`1.1.103`, AST-dump schema stays `1`, ledger `REGEX-0111`. The FIRST grammar consumer of the scope-ancestry `@predicate` primitive `not_in_scope_kind` (`SCOPE-CONTEXT-PREDICATE.1`, landed `PGEN-SCP-0001`) and of the scope-tree `@open_scope`/`@close_scope` directives.

**What / why.** PCRE2 forbids `\K` inside any lookaround body (`pcre2test` 10.47 err 199 "\K is not allowed in lookarounds") — every form (`(?=` `(?!` `(?<=` `(?<!` `(?*` `(?<*` + alpha `(*pla:`…), including when nested inside a group inside the lookaround (`(?=a(b\Kc))`, `((?=x\Ky))`). The released parser already REJECTED all of these, but via the out-of-band validator `find_invalid_keep_out_escape_in_lookaround`, while the GRAMMAR alone ACCEPTED them (`\K`/`keep_out` was an ungated `anchor` branch) — a single-source-of-truth hole. **Behavior-NEUTRAL migration**: the released `--parse` verdict is byte-identical; the reject moves validator→grammar and the standalone validator check is DELETED.

**How (contextual gate, no engine change this slice).** `\K`-in-lookaround is CONTEXTUAL (its legality depends on an enclosing lookaround possibly several groups up), so it needs a whole-active-chain scope-ancestry gate — not the innermost-only `current_scope_is` (misses the nested case) nor the global+monotonic `has_fact` (never retracts → would leak past the lookaround close and reject the valid `(?=ab)\K`). Each of the 7 lookaround rules gains an OPEN-MARKER rule with `@open_scope: {kind: lookaround}` (the marker matches just the opener, since `@open_scope` fires as an effect *after* the rule body — the proven `capture_open` idiom) + `@close_scope: {kind: lookaround}` on the outer rule; `\K` is extracted from `anchor` into a `keep_out` rule carrying `@predicate not_in_scope_kind(lookaround) phase:pre`. The standalone validator check + its 4 exclusive helpers (`lookaround_body_start_at`, `alpha_lookaround_body_start_at`, `is_alpha_lookaround_name`, `find_keep_out_escape`) were DELETED (the `.3.1`/`.3.2`/`.3.16` standalone-deletion precedent); the shared `find_matching_group_end` is kept. The marker's output ($1) is discarded by each parent's `-> {…, body: $2}`, so every accepted lookaround AST is byte-identical.

**Verification (all seeds 0/7/42).** Grammar-only migration test `rust/tests/regex_keep_out_in_lookaround_grammar_migration.rs` GREEN (19 `\K`-in-lookaround forms REJECT + 16 controls ACCEPT, each oracle-verified against `pcre2test` 10.47); released `--parse` 21-case matrix 21/21 byte-identical before→after (behavior-neutral). regex cert `259/259 UNKNOWN=0 fully_certified=true spf=0` (251→259: +8 WITNESSED rules); `--lint-grammar` 0 errors (259 rules); `regex_pcre2_compile_oracle_gate` byte-identical `2189/1867/274/48` (corpus-invisible); `duality_hunt_gate` 9 lanes no new/vanished; `parse_harness_equivalence_gate` regex byte-identical (11 certified); `ast_shape_contract` 4 aligned (inventory 225→232); `parse_harness_combinator_gate` 2/2 + `parse_harness_semantic_gate` 2/2; 37 remaining `regex_compile_validation` unit tests green; `metadata_is_stable` at `1.1.101`/`1.1.103`; clippy source-strict clean. (A pre-existing pathological corpus pattern `((((…(x))))` — catastrophic `capturing_group` backtracking, RGX-0078 — makes the DEBUG oracle probe slow; proven ORTHOGONAL to this slice by construction, its charset is `( ) 0 8 \ x` with no `(?`/`(*`/`\K`.)

## 2026-07-10 - PGEN-SCP-0001 — SCOPE-CONTEXT-PREDICATE.1: the `in_scope_kind` / `not_in_scope_kind` scope-ancestry predicates (a general parser-agnostic engine primitive, proven in isolation)

Parser-agnostic engine primitive — no release/contract/schema bump, inert on every shipped grammar (no consumer references it yet). The direct sibling of the `RULE-SPAN-VALUE-CONSTRAINT` primitive; the shared unlock for `REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY.4.10` (reject `\K` inside a lookaround).

**The gap.** No built-in `@predicate` answered the **lexical-containment** question "am I currently inside an open scope of kind K, at ANY nesting depth?". `current_scope_is` reads only the innermost scope frame (so it misses a token nested inside a plain group inside the target scope); `has_fact`/`lacks_fact` are global and monotonic (`close_scope` never retracts a fact — `semantic_runtime.rs:2706-2748` pops the frame but never truncates `self.facts`), so a fact emitted at construct-OPEN leaks to later siblings; `has_fact_in_current_scope` is depth-exact. The proving consumer — PCRE2's "`\K` is not allowed in lookarounds" (err 199), where `(?=a(b\Kc))` and `((?=x\Ky))` also reject (nested depth) but `(?=ab)\K` accepts (after close) — needs exactly a containment gate that walks the whole enclosing chain and auto-unwinds on close.

**The primitive.** `in_scope_kind(<kind>)` returns `Some(true)` iff any currently-open scope — the innermost frame or any enclosing ancestor up to and including root — has that kind; `not_in_scope_kind(<kind>)` is the boolean complement (the `has_fact`/`lacks_fact` pairing, so "reject X inside Y" needs no `@predicate_def` negation wrapper). Both walk the live `active_chain` via a shared `active_scope_chain_has_kind` helper, so they **auto-unwind** the instant a scope closes — the property facts cannot provide. Registered in `ENGINE_BUILTIN_PREDICATE_NAMES` (no `@predicate_def` may shadow them) and dispatched through the shared `evaluate_predicate`, so both the parse-harness interpreter and the generated parser get them with no codegen change. Kind-only (a name-filtered variant is a documented future extension); a malformed/empty kind is inapplicable (non-blocking), the convention every built-in follows.

**Fix hierarchy (tier-5 engine, tools-first).** Lower tiers were exhausted: the `current_scope_is` route works for regex today only under the fragile, unenforced, non-local invariant "lookarounds are the sole scope-openers" (a `NO WORKAROUNDS` violation); the store's facts are the wrong tool (global+monotonic, no retract-on-close). The active-chain walk is the honest, robust, general expression — and it fills a real platform gap (context-sensitive "reject X inside Y": `\K` in a lookaround, `return` outside a function, `break` outside a loop, a nested-`atomic` ban).

**Verification.** PROVEN IN ISOLATION before any consumer: `in_scope_kind_predicates_walk_the_active_scope_chain` asserts nested-depth TRUE (even under an inner `block` scope where `current_scope_is` is FALSE — the key contrast), post-close auto-unwind FALSE, root-`global` TRUE, malformed None. NO-REGRESSION: `semantic_full_contract_gate` ✅ (semantic differential 80/80 matched, baseline unchanged); `cargo test --lib semantic_runtime` 135/0 + predicate/scope suite 59/0; inert on all shipped grammars; `clippy_on_rust_change` source strict clean; `mdbook_docs_gate` ✅. Book `semantic-store.md` gains a "Scope-context predicates" subsection.

## 2026-07-10 - PGEN-REGEX-PCRE2-0037 — REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY.4.12: collating-element / equivalence-class bracket-tokens are now GRAMMAR-owned (a genuine accepts-invalid correction)

Released regex slice — release `1.1.99`→`1.1.100`, contract `1.1.101`→`1.1.102`, schema `1`, ledger `REGEX-0110`.

**The hole.** A POSIX collating-element `[.….]` or equivalence-class `[=…=]` bracket-token inside a character class is rejected by PCRE2 — err 113 "POSIX collating elements are not supported" as a standalone / member / range-LEFT token, err 150 "invalid range" as a range-RIGHT endpoint. The released parser ACCEPTED all of these at BOTH layers: `class_literal` (via `class_safe_special`) reads a class `[` as a literal `0x5B`, so a `[.`/`[=` token decomposes into a `[` member plus the surrounding `.`/`a`/`=` literal members, and NEITHER the grammar NOR the out-of-band `validate_regex_compile_contract` recognised the token. Unlike the class-range holes `REGEX-0107`/`0108`/`0109` (where the validator did reject), this was a single-source-of-truth **DOUBLE** hole — a genuine accepts-invalid gap, not a masked migration. Ledger `REGEX-0110`; closes the collating/equivalence half of the `.4.5.d` deferred residual.

**Tools-first oracle (verify against the executable oracle, not task-notes).** The `0036` scoping had captured only the range-endpoint err codes; running `pcre2test` 10.47 string-by-string surfaced three subtleties it missed: (1) the opener `[` can be the CLASS-OPENING bracket itself — `[.a.]` (a single leading `[`) is err 113; (2) an opener forms ONLY when `.`/`=` IMMEDIATELY follows `[` — a `^` negation or invisible `\E`/`\Q\E` breaks it (`[^.a.]`, `[\E.a.]` ACCEPT); (3) the content scan is escape-aware and stops at an UNESCAPED `]` (the class close) — `[.].]` ACCEPT (class `[.]` closes at the first `]`), `[.\].]` REJECT (crosses the escaped `\]`), and `\` escapes ONLY `]`, not the terminator dot (`[.a\.]` REJECT).

**The fix (grammar tier — no engine).** A new lookahead-only recognizer `class_bracket_token = "[" class_bracket_token_tail`, with `class_bracket_token_tail = "." ( "\\" "]" | !".]" !"]" builtin_any_char )* ".]" | "=" ( "\\" "]" | !"=]" !"]" builtin_any_char )* "=]"`, blocks the shape at three sites: the MEMBER guard `!class_bracket_token` on `class_member_literal`/`_nocaret` (`-> $2`→`-> $3`; the `.4.6` `[:name:]` idiom); the class-OPEN guard `!class_bracket_token_tail` on `char_class`'s no-caret alternative (`body: $2`→`body: $3`, placed before the `class_zero_width*` prefix so it fires only when `.`/`=` is literally the first char after `[`); and the range-RIGHT `class_atom … "-" … class_bracket_token` alternative on `invalid_class_range` (an ascending `[!-[.a.]]`, not caught by `.4.5.c`'s descending guard). Both rules are referenced only inside `!(…)` ⇒ lookahead-only / PROOF-certified (cert `total` 249→251, proof 7→9).

**Verification.** Behavior-CHANGING at `--parse` (accepts-invalid → PCRE2-convergent reject); every string verified against `pcre2test` 10.47 via `rust/tests/regex_class_bracket_token_grammar_migration.rs` (21 tokens flip ACCEPT→REJECT, 3 descending controls stay REJECT, 23 carve-outs stay ACCEPT). regex cert `251/251 UNKNOWN=0 fully_certified=true spf=0` at seeds 0/7/42; `--lint-grammar` 0 errors (251 rules); `regex_pcre2_compile_oracle_gate` byte-identical `2189/1867/274/48` (collating cells corpus-invisible); `duality_hunt_gate` 9 lanes no new/vanished; `parse_harness_equivalence_gate` regex byte-identical (11 certified); `ast_shape_contract` 18/18 (3 inventory entries re-baselined `$2`→`$3`; accepted-AST byte-identical, count 225); combinator 2/2 + semantic 2/2; regex integration-contract lib tests green (sample counts UNCHANGED 92/26 — contract-sample-invisible, unlike `.4.5.d`). Schema stays `1`.

## 2026-07-09 - PGEN-REGEX-PCRE2-0035 — REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY.4.5.d: the POSIX-class class-range endpoint reject is now GRAMMAR-owned (validator→grammar migration + a PCRE2-convergent correctness fix for the `[[:digit:]-   ]` whitespace subset)

Released regex slice — release `1.1.98`→`1.1.99`, contract `1.1.100`→`1.1.101`, schema `1`, ledger `REGEX-0109`.

**The hole.** A character-class range whose LEFT or RIGHT endpoint is a valid POSIX class (`[:name:]`) is PCRE2 err 150 "invalid range in character class" (`[[:alpha:]-z]` POSIX-left, `[!-[:alpha:]]` POSIX-right). The released parser already REJECTED these, but the reject was owned only by the out-of-band `validate_regex_compile_contract`: the GRAMMAR alone ACCEPTED them, because `class_atom` reads the bracket's `[` as a `class_safe_special` literal `0x5B`, so an ascending `!-[` `class_range` forms and the trailing `:alpha:]` fall through to separate literal members. A single-source-of-truth hole — the POSIX-endpoint sibling of `REGEX-0107`/`.4.5.b` and `REGEX-0108`/`.4.5.c`.

**Tools-first scope.** A grammar-only interpreter residual sweep (`zz_diag_class_range_residual`, run then deleted) over the whole `.4.5` matrix pinned the exact over-accept set: the DESCENDING posix-right cases (`[x-[:alpha:]]`, left code point > `[`=0x5B) ALREADY reject via `.4.5.c`'s `descending_class_range`, so the genuine residual is only the ASCENDING posix-right (`[!-[:alpha:]]`, `!`=33 < `[`=91) and the posix-LEFT (`[[:alpha:]-z]`).

**The fix (grammar tier — no engine).** The `!invalid_class_range` guard (added `.4.5.b`) gains two alternatives referencing the EXISTING positively-reachable `posix_class` rule: `posix_class zw* "-" zw* class_atom` (POSIX left) and `class_atom zw* "-" zw* posix_class` (POSIX right). Because `posix_class` is already positively entered (the first `class_item_core` alternative), NO new rule is created and cert `total` is UNCHANGED (249) — unlike `.4.5.b`/`.4.5.c`. The `class_atom`-after-`-` requirement preserves the trailing-dash carve-out (`[[:alpha:]-]` ACCEPTs — no atom after `-`). One EBNF hazard re-confirmed: a comment line BETWEEN `|` alternatives terminates the rule in the frontend (the two new branches were silently dropped until the comment was moved above the rule and the alternatives made contiguous).

**🔎 NOT fully behavior-neutral — a validator accepts-invalid HOLE surfaced + closed.** The contract-manifest success-sample gate FLIPPED on `[[:digit:]-   ]`. Root cause (a validator/grammar/pcre2 three-way diagnostic, run then deleted): the validator's `dash_is_trailing_literal` (`regex_compile_validation.rs:707`) skips SPACE/TAB/`\Q\E` after the dash and treats it as a literal trailing dash even for a NonLiteral (POSIX) LEFT endpoint, so `[[:digit:]-   ]`/`[[:alpha:]- ]`/`[[:digit:]-\t]` were ACCEPTED by the released parser where `pcre2test` 10.47 rejects err 150. This slice flips that whitespace subset **ACCEPT→REJECT** at `--parse` — a genuine PCRE2-convergent correctness fix — while staying behavior-neutral for every other posix-endpoint case (the validator already rejected). PERFECTLY PCRE2-convergent: the zero-width carve-out `[[:alpha:]-\Q\E]` stays ACCEPT (no over-reject). One contract success sample (`[[:digit:]-   ]`) moved to failure (counts 93/25→92/26). Every accepted AST byte-identical (schema stays `1`).

**Scope + what stays validator-owned.** VALID-POSIX-name endpoints only. The collating (`[.a.]`) / equivalence (`[=a=]`) bracket-token endpoints (`[!-[.a.]]`, `[!-[=a=]]`) have no grammar recognizer yet (they join `.4.12`), and the quoted/`\u{}`/bare-whitespace-endpoint descending cases stay validator-owned; the `find_invalid_char_class_construct` range-check is DELETED only once the whole class-range family is grammar-owned.

**Verification.** Integration test (`rust/tests/regex_class_range_posix_grammar_migration.rs`) — posix-endpoint cells (incl. the whitespace flip subset) flip grammar ACCEPT→REJECT, the `.4.5.c` descending posix-right stays REJECT (regression pin), carve-outs (incl. `[[:alpha:]-\Q\E]`) stay ACCEPT; every string verified against `pcre2test` 10.47. regex cert `249/249 UNKNOWN=0 fully_certified spf=0` ×seeds 0/7/42 (UNCHANGED — no new rule). `--lint-grammar` 0 errors (249 rules). `regex_pcre2_compile_oracle_gate` byte-identical `2189/1867/274/48` (flip cells corpus-invisible; the contract manifest caught them). `duality_hunt_gate` 9 lanes no new/vanished. `parse_harness_equivalence_gate` regex byte-identical. `ast_shape_contract` inventory 225 UNCHANGED (no new `->` shape). combinator + semantic gates ✅. 18 regex integration-contract lib tests green (metadata counts re-pinned 92/26). version drift gate `1.1.99`/`1.1.101` match ledger.

## 2026-07-09 - PGEN-REGEX-PCRE2-0034 — REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY.4.5.c: the non-`[` DESCENDING literal class-range reject is now GRAMMAR-owned (behavior-NEUTRAL validator→grammar migration)

Released regex slice — release `1.1.97`→`1.1.98`, contract `1.1.99`→`1.1.100`, schema `1`, ledger `REGEX-0108`.

**The hole.** A character-class range of two LITERAL endpoints whose left code point exceeds the right is PCRE2 err 108 "range out of order in character class" (`[z-a]`, `[9-0]`, `[\x39-\x30]`, `[\x{100}-a]`). The released parser already REJECTED these, but the reject was owned only by the out-of-band `validate_regex_compile_contract`: the GRAMMAR alone ACCEPTED them, because `class_range` forms for any two literals and its `@validate: ord($1)<=ord($5)` is a non-parse-gating codegen annotation (proven `.4.5.a`). A single-source-of-truth hole — the descending-literal sibling of `REGEX-0107`/`.4.5.b`.

**The fix (grammar tier — consumes the RSVC.3 engine primitive).** The `!invalid_class_range` guard gains a THIRD alternative `descending_class_range = class_range_endpoint zw* "-" zw* class_range_endpoint`, gated by `@predicate { name: value_compare_codepoint, args: [$1, gt, $5], phase: post }` (`RULE-SPAN-VALUE-CONSTRAINT.3`, `PGEN-RSVC-0003`, committed `20bc0462`): it decodes each RAW endpoint spelling (bare non-whitespace literal + `\xHH`/`\x{}`/`\NNN`/`\o{}`/`\cX`/named escapes) to its Unicode code point and matches when left > right. The braced `[\x{100}-a]` is the code-point discriminator — a textual compare (`\`=92 < `a`=97) would wrongly ACCEPT; only decoding (256 > 97) rejects. `class_range_endpoint = class_range_decodable_atom -> $text` re-emits the raw spelling (a bare `class_atom` ref would give a typed `{type:escape}` object whose `scalar_text` is `None` → non-blocking → over-accept). `class_range_decodable_atom` is restricted to DECODABLE, NON-WHITESPACE endpoints.

**A tools-first in-slice regression (root-caused + fixed before release).** The first grammar layer passed cert 249/249 and the descending test but the `regex_pcre2_compile_oracle_gate` caught a false_reject `48→50` — a bare WHITESPACE endpoint reaches the `post` predicate with an EMPTY raw spelling (`value_compare_codepoint("" > "!") → None`, proven by runtime trace + the interpreter before/after bisect, in EITHER endpoint slot), so the gate went inapplicable → non-blocking → `descending_class_range` matched and OVER-BLOCKED ascending whitespace ranges (`[ -!]`, `[ --]`, `[\t-a]`). Every non-whitespace literal AND every escape spelling (`\x20`/`\t`/`\040`) resolves correctly — only the bare whitespace literal empties (a GENERAL latent pipeline finding, `docs/decisions/project_dollar_text_whitespace_empty_in_predicate_arg.md`). FIX: `class_range_decodable_atom = class_range_decodable_escape | letter | digit | class_safe_special | unicode_char` drops the `whitespace` branch, so `descending_class_range` never forms for a bare-whitespace endpoint — the range stays validator-owned. Oracle restored to `2189/1867/274/48`.

**Behavior-NEUTRAL downstream.** The released `--parse` verdict is byte-identical to `1.1.97` (the validator still rejects descending ranges via err 108), so the migration is observable only at the grammar layer. Every accepted AST is byte-identical (schema stays `1`).

**Verification.** Grammar-only integration test (`rust/tests/regex_class_range_descending_grammar_migration.rs`) — 10 descending ranges flip grammar ACCEPT→REJECT, ascending/equal/carve-out/whitespace controls stay ACCEPT. regex cert `249/249 UNKNOWN=0 fully_certified spf=0` ×seeds 0/7/42 (245→249: +4 lookahead-only PROOF rules). `--lint-grammar` 0 errors (249 rules). `regex_pcre2_compile_oracle_gate` byte-identical `2189/1867/274/48`. `duality_hunt_gate` 9 lanes no new/vanished. `parse_harness_equivalence_gate` regex byte-identical. `ast_shape_contract` inventory 224→225 aligned. combinator 27/27 + semantic 33/33. version drift gate `1.1.98`/`1.1.100` match ledger. SCOPE: decodable non-whitespace descending literal ranges only; POSIX-left, `-[`-right, and quoted/`\u{}`/bare-whitespace-endpoint descending stay validator-owned pending `.4.5.d` (which deletes the `find_invalid_char_class_construct` range-check).

## 2026-07-09 - PGEN-RSVC-0003 — RULE-SPAN-VALUE-CONSTRAINT.3: the code-point-coercion sibling builtin `value_compare_codepoint` (ENGINE primitive, proven in isolation)

Engine-only slice — no parser EBNF touched, so no contract/ledger/release bump (the primitive is inert until a grammar adopts it).

**What.** A new general `@predicate` built-in `value_compare_codepoint` — the sibling of `value_compare` that compares its two operands by their decoded **Unicode code point** instead of as integer/textual values. Same op words (`lt`·`le`·`gt`·`ge`·`eq`·`ne`), same payload references; the difference is coercion: each operand is decoded as a single character literal — a bare Unicode scalar or the standard C/Perl char-escape vocabulary (hex `\xHH` / `\x{H..}`, octal `\o{O..}` / `\NNN`, control `\cX`, named `\a \b \e \f \n \r \t`, or a backslash-escaped literal `\X`) — to its code point, then the two code points are compared numerically.

**Why.** This is the "codepoint-decoding coercion mode" the `value_compare` v1 (RULE-SPAN-VALUE-CONSTRAINT.2) explicitly deferred as "a later, separate widening leaf." It is the enabler for `REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY.4.5.c` (migrating the class-range descending-order reject `[z-a]` / `[\x{100}-z]`, PCRE2 err 108, from the out-of-band validator into the grammar): tools-first `--parse-dump-ast-pretty` showed class-range endpoints reach a rule-span predicate as RAW spellings via positional `$N`, and a textual/`i64` `value_compare` mis-orders them (`"\x{100}"` sorts textually *before* `"\x{FF}"` — `'1' < 'F'` — though the code points are `256 > 255`).

**How (design).** A SIBLING built-in, not a `value_compare` mode/flag — chosen over a `coerce: codepoint` payload key (which would touch the shared `SemanticPredicateSpec` every construction site builds) and over auto-coercion inside `compare_values` (which would silently change the proven `value_compare`/`counted_quantifier` path). One dispatch arm + one registry line (the exact pattern `.2` used), zero blast radius. The decoder is a GENERAL character-literal decoder (nothing regex-specific), but its numeric results match the regex compile contract's `class_escape_literal_codepoint` on well-formed inputs, so the regex consumer gets PCRE2-faithful ordering. Codegen / interpreter / grammar unchanged (both call the shared runtime; args are generic → byte-identical by construction).

**Verification.** Direct decoder unit tests (`decode_char_literal_to_codepoint_covers_the_char_escape_vocabulary` + `compare_codepoints_orders_by_decoded_scalar_not_text`). `parse_harness_semantic_gate` GREEN: `sem_value_compare_codepoint CLEAN samples=8 diverge=0 anchor_miss=0` — all six ops each verdict-changing over hex/octal/control/named endpoints, code-point-vs-textual discriminators (`\x{FF}`vs`\x{100}`; `\a`==`\x07`; descending literal `z-a`), and a `None`-non-blocking anchor (`\x{}`) — interpreter == compile-and-run oracle byte-identical; all 32 prior constructs still CLEAN. `parse_harness_equivalence_gate` GREEN (the 11 certified grammars byte-identical — the builtin is inert on every shipped grammar). Full dual lib suite + clippy source-clean.

## 2026-07-09 - PGEN-REGEX-PCRE2-0033 — REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY.4.5.b: the non-`[` NONLITERAL class-range reject is now GRAMMAR-owned (behavior-NEUTRAL validator→grammar migration)

Released regex slice — release `1.1.96`→`1.1.97`, contract `1.1.98`→`1.1.99`, schema `1`, ledger `REGEX-0107`.

**The hole.** A character-class range whose LEFT or RIGHT endpoint is a NONLITERAL shorthand (`\d \D \h \H \s \S \v \V \w \W`) or property (`\p…` / `\P…`) escape is PCRE2 err 150 "invalid range" (`[\d-x]`, `[a-\d]`, `[\p{Lu}-x]`, `[a-\p{Lu}]`). The released parser already REJECTED these, but the reject was owned only by the out-of-band `validate_regex_compile_contract`: the GRAMMAR alone ACCEPTED them, because `class_atom` (the range-endpoint reader) excludes the shorthand/property escapes, so `class_range` never forms and `[\d-x]` splits into three members (`\d`, `-`, `x`). A single-source-of-truth hole — the EBNF did not encode the rule.

**The fix (grammar tier, no engine).** A zero-width negative lookahead `!invalid_class_range` guards the three class-item positions (`class_item` / `class_item_visible` / `class_item_visible_nocaret`) via `*_core` passthrough rules (`-> $2` — a NAMED core rule, not an inline `(…)` group which corrupts positional refs → `<invalid_sequence_access>`, per `feedback_quantified_group_extraction`). `invalid_class_range` recognizes two shapes: nonliteral-LEFT `<nl> - <endpoint>` and literal-LEFT/nonliteral-RIGHT `<atom> - <nl>`, where `<nl>` = `class_range_nonliteral_atom` = `"\\" (shorthand | property_escape)`. Shape 1's right side must be a real endpoint atom (not `]`), so the literal-dash carve-out `[\d-]` stays ACCEPT; the `-` is a BARE terminal, so `[\d\-x]`'s escaped dash stays a member. `invalid_class_range` + its helpers are referenced only inside `!(…)`, so certificate-coverage certifies them by PROOF (lookahead-only / positively-unreachable). SCOPE: shorthand + property endpoints only — POSIX-left (`[[:alpha:]-z]`) and the `-[`-right cases (`.4.5.a`) stay validator-owned pending `.4.5.c`, when the `find_invalid_char_class_construct` range-check is deleted.

**Behavior-NEUTRAL downstream.** The released `--parse` verdict is byte-identical to `1.1.96` (the validator still rejects), so the migration is observable only at the grammar layer (the certified interpreter, which runs the grammar without the validator). Every accepted AST is byte-identical (schema stays `1`).

**Verification.** Grammar-only integration test (`rust/tests/regex_class_range_nonliteral_grammar_migration.rs`) — 23 invalid ranges flip grammar ACCEPT→REJECT, 16 carve-outs stay ACCEPT, 22 valid class ASTs byte-identical interp==gen. regex cert `245/245 UNKNOWN=0 fully_certified spf=0` ×seeds 0/7/42 (239→245: +3 witnessed `*_core`, +3 lookahead-only PROOF rules). `--lint-grammar` 0 errors (245 rules). Released `--parse` matrix 28/28 unchanged. `regex_pcre2_compile_oracle_gate` byte-identical `2189/1867/274/48`. `duality_hunt_gate` 9 lanes no new/vanished. `parse_harness_equivalence_gate` regex byte-identical. `ast_shape_contract` inventory 221→224 aligned. combinator 27/27 + semantic 32/32. version drift gate `1.1.97`/`1.1.99` match ledger.

## 2026-07-09 - PGEN-REGEX-PCRE2-0032 — REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY.4.5.a.1: the `\v` / `\V` class-range accepts-invalid FIX (a genuine correctness fix, sibling of REGEX-0105; NOT a neutral migration)

Released regex slice — release `1.1.95`→`1.1.96`, contract `1.1.97`→`1.1.98`, schema `1`, ledger `REGEX-0106`.

**The bug.** The vertical-whitespace shorthands `\v` / `\V` were treated as LITERAL class-range endpoints, so
`[\v-x]`, `[\V-x]`, `[a-\v]` were **accepts-invalid** — the released parser (grammar AND the out-of-band
validator) BOTH accepted patterns `pcre2test` 10.47 rejects err 150 "invalid range". Surfaced while mapping
the COMPLETE nonliteral class-range endpoint set for the (deferred) `.4.5.b` grammar migration.

**Root cause (WHY + WHERE), two halves.** (validator) `regex_compile_validation.rs::is_nonliteral_class_escape`
enumerated the nonliteral shorthands `\d \D \h \H \s \S \w \W` (+ `\p` `\P`) but OMITTED `\v` / `\V`, so a
`\v` / `\V` range endpoint fell through to `class_escape_literal_codepoint`'s `_ => next as u32` and decoded
to literal `118` / `86` (an ascending range that accepted). (grammar) `grammars/regex.ebnf`'s
`class_range_literal_escape_letter_strict` listed `v` / `V`, so `\v` / `\V` formed a `class_range` endpoint —
feeding the validator's mis-read AND letting the store-aware generator emit `\v`-ranges. The already-correct
horizontal analogs `\h` / `\H` are handled the right way (members only, never range endpoints).

**The fix (GRAMMAR + VALIDATOR tier — make `\v` / `\V` byte-identical to `\h` / `\H`).** (1) drop `'V'` / `'v'`
from `class_range_literal_escape_letter_strict` (members via `class_simple_escape` untouched ⇒ `[\v]` / `[\V]`
stay valid; no longer generated as range endpoints ⇒ duality-safe); (2) add `b'v' | b'V'` to
`is_nonliteral_class_escape` ⇒ err-150 reject. Hex/octal endpoints of the same code point (`[\x0b-\x0c]`,
`[\013-\014]`) stay literal and valid — only the shorthand form is nonliteral. A validator-only fix was
rejected: it would leave the generator emitting `\v`-ranges the corrected validator rejects (a new duality
break); the grammar half is required. The class-range validity family stays validator-owned pending the
deferred `.4.5.b` / `.4.5.c` grammar migration (which now covers a uniformly-correct nonliteral family).

**Behavior change (NOT neutral).** `[\v-x]`, `[\V-x]`, `[a-\v]` flip ACCEPT→REJECT (`E_PARSE_FAILURE` — match
on code, not text). `[a-\V]` stays REJECT (was err-108 descending, now err-150 nonliteral). Members + hex/octal
ranges + all other cells byte-identical, both profiles.

**Verified.** Full release-probe matrix == `pcre2test` 10.47 (0 divergences). `regex_pcre2_compile_oracle_gate`
byte-identical `2189/1867/274/48` (the corpus has no `\v` / `\V` class-range cells — corpus-invisible, proven
by the direct oracle sweep + the new validator unit pin `rejects_vertical_whitespace_shorthand_class_range_endpoints`,
the same class as `.3.21`). regex cert `239/239/0 fully_certified spf=0` ×seeds 0/7/42 (UNCHANGED); `--lint-grammar`
0 errors (239 rules); `duality_hunt_gate` 9 lanes NO new/vanished signature; `parse_harness_equivalence_gate`
regex byte-identical; `ast_shape_contract` inventory 221 UNCHANGED. Lockstep: ledger `REGEX-0106`, consts
`1.1.96` / `1.1.98`, tracked contract JSON, contract Identity + Highlights, regex book (validator + changelog +
`rules-char-class` + HTML), top book parser-families chain, the tree + `docs/TASK_TREE.md` + `MEMORY.md` +
`LIVE_ACHIEVEMENT_STATUS.md` + `DEVELOPMENT_NOTES.md`.

## 2026-07-09 - PGEN-REGEX-PCRE2-0031 — REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY.4.5.a: the `-[` / `-||` class-range accepts-invalid FIX (a genuine correctness fix, NOT a neutral migration)

Released regex slice — release `1.1.94`→`1.1.95`, contract `1.1.96`→`1.1.97`, schema `1`, ledger `REGEX-0105`.

**The bug.** Inside a NORMAL character class, a RANGE whose right endpoint begins with `[` or `||` was
**accepts-invalid** — the released parser (grammar AND the out-of-band validator) BOTH accepted patterns
PCRE2 10.47 rejects: `[a-[b]]`/`[z-[a]]`/`[a-[]`/`[~-||]`/`[}-||]` (err 108 descending) and
`[x-[:alpha:]]`/`[a-[:digit:]]`/`[a-[.-.]]`/`[!-[:alpha:]]`/`[\d-[z]]`/`[\d-||z]` (err 150 nonliteral).
`[!-[]` (both endpoints ascending literals) masked the bug — it accepts on both.

**Root cause (WHY + WHERE).** `regex_compile_validation.rs::scan_char_class`'s two range branches gated
range detection on `!dash_starts_alt_extended_class_operator(bytes, dash)`, which suppressed the range
whenever the char after `-` was `[` or `||`. That guard belongs to PCRE2's ALTERNATE extended-class syntax
`(?[...])`, but `scan_char_class` is dispatched ONLY for NORMAL classes (`!is_extended_class_start`), where
`-[`/`-||` is ALWAYS a range — so the guard was unconditionally mis-scoped. `--parse-dump-ast-pretty`
PROVED the grammar already forms the `class_range` correctly (the `.4.5` investigation's grammar-side note
was imprecise) — the divergence is ENTIRELY the validator.

**Fix (VALIDATOR tier).** The class-range validity family stays validator-owned pending the deferred
`.4.5.b`/`.4.5.c` grammar migration (which need PEG-ordering + a `value_compare` codepoint-widening
primitive); `.4.5.a` is the cheap structural correctness fix sequenced first. (1) Removed
`!dash_starts_alt_extended_class_operator(...)` from both range branches + deleted the function; (2) added
`scan_class_bracket_token` (recognizes `[:..:]`/`[...]`/`[=..=]` by scanning to the first `:]`/`.]`/`=]`),
checked first in `read_substantive_class_atom`, so a bracket-token right endpoint classifies NON-LITERAL →
err 150. A bare `[` still reads the literal `0x5B` and orders normally, so ascending `-[` ranges (`[!-[]`)
stay ACCEPT. NO grammar / codegen / generated-parser change.

**Verification.** `regex_pcre2_compile_oracle_gate` NET IMPROVEMENT, true-measured `2189/1867/274/48` (was
`2189/1858/285/46`): ~11 DEFAULT-mode `-[`/`-[.`/`-[=` accepts-invalid corpus cells now correctly reject
(false_accept 285→274). The 2 new false-rejects `[\d-[z]]`/`[\d-||z]` carry the `alt_extended_class`
modifier (`PCRE2_ALT_EXTENDED_CLASS`, a non-default mode PGEN does not model — same documented divergence
class as the existing `[A--B]` class-set-operation false-rejects), ratchet 46→48, env v11→v12. cert-coverage
`239/239 UNKNOWN=0 fully_certified=true spf=0` seeds 0/7/42 (UNCHANGED); `--lint-grammar` 0 errors (239
rules); `duality_hunt_gate` 9 lanes NO new signature; equivalence byte-identical; ast_shape 221 UNCHANGED.
New pin `regex_class_range_bracket_endpoint_rejects_pcre2_faithfully` + validator test
`rejects_bracket_token_class_range_endpoints`; the stale `1.1.27` test that locked in the bug DELETED.

**🔎 New divergence found + tracked (`.4.12`, NOT fixed here):** STANDALONE collating `[[.a.]]` /
equivalence `[[=a=]]` MEMBERS are PCRE2 err 113 but PGEN accepts — a distinct class (err 113 vs the range
err 150/108) needing its own recognizer.

`x{5,4}`) — the last min>max residual of the out-of-band compile-contract validator — is migrated into

the general RULE-SPAN `value_compare` `@predicate` primitive (RULE-SPAN-VALUE-CONSTRAINT.2), and the 12th
validator→grammar migration.

- **Grammar** (`grammars/regex.ebnf`): the `{n,m}` range form is extracted into a dedicated
  `counted_quantifier_range` rule gated by `@predicate: { name: value_compare, args: [$min, le, $max],
  phase: post, view: shaped }` — a cross-capture comparison of the produced `{min,max}` fields
  (decimal-integer numeric, so `{05,4}` = 5>4 REJECTS while `{05,5}` = 5≤5 ACCEPTS). A `post` rejection is
  backtrackable, so a min>max range loses its branch, no other body branch fully-consumes the brace, and
  the `literal_open_brace` guard's `digit+` lookahead blocks the literal fallback ⇒ whole-pattern REJECT,
  err-104-faithful (no guard change).
- **🔎 Tool-surfaced design pivot.** The initial raw-view positional gate `[$1, le, $5]` hard-errored
  ("could not resolve attribute reference '$1'", tool-traced via `--trace-rules`): this rule's own `->`
  shapes its content to JSON, and the raw-content capture for a Raw-view post-predicate is **not emitted**
  on the sequence-with-return-transform codegen path, so a positional ref cannot resolve. Fixed by using
  the proven SV `view: shaped` idiom with NAMED refs to the produced `{min,max}` fields — robust to that
  AND to the unmatched `brace_ws?` optionals. (The codegen raw-capture gap is a latent limitation noted for
  a future engine leaf — see the surfaced-findings callout in the task leaf.)
- **Validator** (`rust/src/regex_compile_validation.rs`): `find_invalid_counted_quantifier` +
  `validate_counted_quantifier_body` (both min>max-only) + 3 unit tests DELETED; parity pin
  `regex_counted_quantifier_order_rejects_at_the_grammar_layer_pcre2_faithfully` ADDED in `parser_registry.rs`.
- **Duality-neutral (proven empirically).** The generator emits `{0,0}` for range forms (0 min>max in a
  3000-sample plain generation, seeds 0/7/42) and the 2000-sample directed duality hunt surfaces only the
  start-option signature; parse-time `@predicate` is not honored generation-side, so the migration leaves
  generation byte-identical — no `@gen_predicate` companion needed.
- **Behavior-neutral**: every input's accept/reject verdict is byte-identical to `1.1.93`; the only
  observable change is the rejection message (`E_PARSE_FAILURE` code unchanged). AST-dump schema stays `1`
  (the `{min,max}` shape is preserved through the extracted rule).
- **Versions**: regex release `1.1.93`→`1.1.94` / integration contract `1.1.95`→`1.1.96` / schema `1`;
  ledger `REGEX-0104`.
- **Verified**: `pcre2test` 10.47 matrix (6 reject + 8 accept, message-source probe grammar-layer-confirmed);
  regex cert `total=239 witness=239 UNKNOWN=0 fully_certified=true spf=0` at seeds 0/7/42 (238→239, the new

  regex byte-identical; `regex_ast_shape_contract_gate` aligned (inventory 220→221); dual `--lib` suite;

captures (a RULE-SPAN constraint, distinct from the ATOM-scoped `@range`/`@len`/`@enum`/`@regex`

generated parser and the interpreter (both call the shared semantic runtime).

  grammar unchanged (shared runtime; args generic).

  `compare_predicate_values` makes `eq`/`ne` **textual** (so `"05" != "5"`) while the ordering ops are

## 2026-07-09 - PGEN-REGEX-PCRE2-0027 — REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY.4.2: `\k`/group NAME validity is GRAMMAR-owned (RELEASED regex slice: release 1.1.92→1.1.93 / contract 1.1.94→1.1.95, schema 1, ledger REGEX-0103)

The design-focused session the `.4.2` SCOPING called for. Tool-backed design (`pcre2test` 10.47): a name is
capped at 128 **code units** (err 148) UNIFORMLY in every position (defs + `\g`/`(?&`/`(?P=`/`\k`/condition
refs); the code-unit is byte@8-bit / code-point@32-bit. RGX is Unicode-only, so the faithful limit is **128
code points**, which PGEN's `name` counts natively ⇒ a pure-grammar `{0,127}` bound (BOUNDED-QUANT.1), **no
new primitive**. Three STRUCTURAL/DECLARATIVE grammar edits (fix-hierarchy GRAMMAR tier):

- **`name` bounded `{0,127}`** (was `*`) — every name ≤ 128 code-points, matching PCRE2 err 148.
- **`\k` is always a named-backref introducer** — `!"k"` on `simple_escape` + `'k'` dropped from
  `simple_escape_letter_strict` (the `.4.1` `\p`/`\P` precedent), so bare `\k`/`\kabc` (err 169) and empty
  `\k''`/`\k<>`/`\k{}` (err 162) hard-REJECT at the grammar layer in BOTH profiles.
- **`\k'name'` quote branch added** to `backreference` (the angle/braced forms already existed).

`regex_compile_validation.rs::find_invalid_named_escape_or_group_name` + its 5 exclusive helpers +
`PCRE2_MAX_NAME_SIZE` + 3 unit tests DELETED (11th validator→grammar migration; 4th `.4` deletion-prep child;
the function is fully retired). New pin `parser_registry::regex_named_names_reject_at_the_grammar_layer_pcre2_faithfully`.

**Two fidelity refinements (NOT byte-neutral):** (a) `\k'name'` was silently mis-parsed as shorthand-`k` +
`'`/`n`/`'` literals (accepted, WRONG shape) — now a proper `{type:"backreference",kind:"named"}`; (b) a
non-ASCII name of 65–128 code points is now ACCEPT (was validator-REJECT under 8-bit BYTE counting) — the
Unicode-only-faithful behavior. Pure-ASCII names byte-identical; AST-dump schema stays `1`.

Verified: cert `238/238/UNKNOWN=0` seeds 0/7/42; oracle byte-identical `2189/1858/285/46`; duality 9 lanes no
new sig; differential-equiv regex byte-identical (CERTIFIED); ast_shape inventory 219→220 aligned; dual `--lib`
suite `887/0`; `--lint-grammar` 0 errors. Books/contract/ledger in lockstep.

## 2026-07-09 - PGEN-REGEX-PCRE2-0026 — REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY.4.2 SCOPING (PURE-DOCS, no code/version change)

Tools-first scoping of the `\k`/group-NAME-validity leaf before any edit (message-source probe both
profiles + grammar read), recorded in the tree so the next session starts with the design framed.

- **Named-group charset is ALREADY grammar-owned** — `name` (`regex.ebnf:528`) rejects `(?<1bad>x)`/
  `(?<>x)`/`(?'1bad'x)`/`(?P<1bad>x)`/`(?<a b>x)` at the grammar layer (probe: GRAMMAR-reject). No-op.
- **`\k` shape + non-empty name is load-bearing** — `\k`/`\kabc`/`\k''`/`\k<>`/`\k{}` are VALIDATOR-reject
  (grammar accepts). Structural: route `\k` through a delimited non-empty `name`.
- **Length ≤128 is load-bearing (both) + a design question** — 129-char `(?<…>x)`/`\k<…>` are
  VALIDATOR-reject (`name` is unbounded `*`). A bounded quantifier `{0,127}` (BOUNDED-QUANT.1) covers ASCII,
  but PCRE2's limit is 128 CODE UNITS / the validator uses BYTE `name.len()` while `{0,127}` counts CHARS —
  they diverge for multi-byte Unicode names. Needs a deliberate design pass (Unicode-aware code-unit bound
  vs a byte-length primitive, justified per the fix hierarchy) → best in a fresh design-focused session.

## 2026-07-09 - PGEN-REGEX-PCRE2-0025 — REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY.4.4: escape-in-class rejects are now grammar-owned (behavior-neutral validator→grammar migration; release `1.1.92`/`1.1.94`/schema `1`, ledger REGEX-0102)

Session #75. RELEASED regex slice (grammar + regen + validator deletion + full lockstep), the 3rd `.4`
deletion-prep child of the re-scoped capstone (the 10th compile-contract check migrated into the EBNF).
TOOLBOX-FIRST throughout.

- **Root cause (tool-backed, message-source probe).** PCRE2 forbids `\A \B \C \G \K \R \X \Z \z` as a
  character-class member and allows `\N` only in its braced form `\N{…}`; the GRAMMAR alone accepted them
  all — `[\B]` via the `class_simple_escape` catch-all, `[\C]` via `single_byte_escape`, and
  `[\A-x]`/`[\z-\x{FFFF}]` via the range path. The reject lived only in the out-of-band
  `find_invalid_char_class_construct` (`read_class_atom`) — a single-source-of-truth hole.
- **Fix (grammar tier, no engine).** 10 guards `!"A" !"B" !"C" !"G" !"K" !"R" !"X" !"Z" !"z" !( "N" !"{" )`
  on both `class_simple_escape` variants (`char:$23`/`$17`); `single_byte_escape` dropped from
  `class_escape_unit` (kept in `escape_unit` for the pattern body); `A`/`G`/`z` dropped from
  `class_range_literal_escape_letter_strict` (range-endpoint reachable). `!( "N" !"{" )` keeps `\N{…}` valid.
  The two `read_class_atom` reject blocks + 3 validator unit tests deleted; a `parser_registry.rs` pin added.
- **Behavior-neutral (proven).** Message-source probe: 18 reject forms flip VALIDATOR-reject→GRAMMAR-reject
  (both profiles), 20 controls + 8 pattern-body forms stay ACCEPT. Oracle byte-identical `2189/1858/285/46`;
  cert `238/238/UNKNOWN=0` at seeds 0/7/42; duality 9 lanes no new/vanished signature; differential-equiv
  byte-identical; ast_shape aligned (manifest `$7`→`$17` / `$13`→`$23`, text-only positional bump). Reject
  CODE stays `E_PARSE_FAILURE` — only the message moves validator→grammar.

## 2026-07-09 - PGEN-REGEX-PCRE2-0024 — REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY.4.6: POSIX character-class NAME validity is now grammar-owned (behavior-neutral validator→grammar migration; release `1.1.91`/`1.1.93`/schema `1`, ledger REGEX-0101)

Session #74. RELEASED regex slice (grammar + regen + full lockstep), the 2nd `.4` deletion-prep child of
the re-scoped capstone (the 9th compile-contract check migrated into the EBNF). TOOLBOX-FIRST throughout.

- **Root cause (tool-backed, message-source probe).** The GRAMMAR alone accepted an unknown POSIX class name
  (`[[:foo:]]`/`[a[:<:]]`/`[[::]]`/`[x[:foo:]y]`/`[^[:foo:]]`): `posix_class` fails on a name outside the
  14-name set, so the `[`/`:`/letters fall back to `class_literal` and `char_class` closes as literals. The
  reject lived only in the out-of-band validator `find_invalid_char_class_construct` → `is_valid_posix_class_name`
  — a single-source-of-truth hole ([[project_ebnf_is_single_source_of_truth]]).
- **Fix (grammar tier, no engine).** The class-member `[` literal is guarded by an inline negative lookahead for
  the `[:…:]` posix-token shape (`!( "[:" "^"? ( !":]" builtin_any_char )* ":]" )`) at the 3 member positions
  (`class_item`, `class_item_visible`, `class_item_visible_nocaret`) via two new wrapper rules
  `class_member_literal` / `class_member_literal_nocaret` (`-> $2`, the `literal_open_brace` precedent).
  Name-agnostic: a valid name is won by `posix_class` (longest-match), an invalid name blocks the `[` literal so
  the class cannot close → grammar-REJECT. `is_valid_posix_class_name` + its call + 2 validator unit tests deleted;
  `scan_posix_class` recognition retained for range analysis (`.4.5`).
- **Behavior-neutral.** The guard scans to the first `:]` exactly like the deleted validator, so every accept/reject
  verdict is byte-identical to `1.1.90` (both profiles); only the reject MESSAGE moves validator→grammar.
- **Verified.** 33-cell matrix 100% == `pcre2test` 10.47; 4 contract-pinned POSIX AST shapes byte-identical; regex
  cert 238/238/0 spf=0 ×seeds 0/7/42 (236→238, 2 net-new rules witnessed); oracle gate byte-identical
  `2189/1858/285/46` (a first `!"]"` PCRE2-exact attempt regressed +1 false-accept on the escaped-`]` case
  `[abc[:x\]pqr:]]` — reverted); duality 9 lanes no new signature; equivalence gate regex byte-identical;
  ast_shape 217→219 aligned; dual lib suite 891/0; new pin `regex_posix_class_names_reject_at_the_grammar_layer_pcre2_faithfully`.
- **Honest bound (pre-existing).** The scan crosses both escaped/unescaped `]` (like the validator); PCRE2 stops at
  an unescaped `]` (`[x[:foo]bar:]y]` accepts in PCRE2, rejects in PGEN both before/after) — a PCRE2-exact `]`-boundary follow-up.

## 2026-07-09 - PGEN-REGEX-PCRE2-0023 (REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY.4.1): the bare `\p`/`\P` Unicode-property escape is now GRAMMAR-owned — behavior-neutral validator→grammar migration (regex release `1.1.89`→`1.1.90`, contract `1.1.91`→`1.1.92`, schema `1`, ledger REGEX-0100)

Session #73. A RELEASED regex slice (grammar edit + regen + full lockstep), the first `.4` deletion-prep
child. Encodes the bare Unicode-property-escape acceptance rule into `grammars/regex.ebnf`, migrating
`regex_compile_validation.rs::find_invalid_property_escape` out of the out-of-band validator — the EBNF is
now the single source of truth for it.

**Root cause (tool-backed, message-source probe).** In PCRE2 `\p`/`\P` are ALWAYS Unicode-property
introducers — a bare (un-braced) one MUST be a valid one-letter general category (`\pL`) or the `{name}`
form, else it is a compile error. The GRAMMAR alone previously ACCEPTED a bad bare form: on `\pA`,
`property_escape`'s `"p" short_prop_letter` branch fails (`A` ∉ the 14 category letters), the longest-match
tournament falls through to `simple_escape`, whose `simple_escape_letter_strict` positive set listed `'P'`
and `'p'`, so `\p` matched as a shorthand + `A` as a literal. In class context `class_simple_escape_
{strict,relaxed}` guarded only the braced `!"p{"`/`!"P{"`, so `[\pA]` leaked identically. The rejection
lived ONLY in the out-of-band `find_invalid_property_escape` — proven by a message-source probe: on the
`1.1.89` release probe `\pA` rejected with the VALIDATOR message (`\p without braces must use a one-letter
Unicode general category`), which fires only AFTER a grammar-accept.

**Fix (grammar tier, no engine).** `'P'`/`'p'` DROPPED from `simple_escape_letter_strict` (positive
exclusion, generation-faithful — the `.3.13`/`.3.19`/`.3.23` idiom), and the `!"p{"`/`!"P{"` guards
BROADENED to whole-letter `!"p"`/`!"P"` on `simple_escape` + both `class_simple_escape` variants
(positional-safe: `$5`/`$13`/`$7` unchanged). `find_invalid_property_escape` + its call site + its 2 unit
tests DELETED (`is_short_unicode_property_letter` retained — `skip_regex_escape` still uses it for the
other checks). 7 of the 8 validator check families remain (capstone `.4` deletes the rest via `.4.2`..`.4.11`).

**Behavior-NEUTRAL downstream.** Every input's accept/reject verdict is byte-identical to `1.1.89` (the
validator rejected these before, the grammar rejects them now, in BOTH profiles). The only observable
change is the rejection MESSAGE (validator text → `E_PARSE_FAILURE`). After: `\pA`/`\P_`/`\p`/`\P`/`[\pA]`/
`a\pAb`/`x\p` REJECT via the grammar (`Parser did not consume full input`); `\pL`/`\PN`/`\pl`/`\Pn`/`\pC`/
`\pZ`/`[\pL\PN]`/`\p{Lu}`/`\P{Han}`/`[\p{L}]` ACCEPT (unchanged).

**Verification.** message-source before→after; regex cert `236/236/0 fully_certified spf=0` ×seeds 0/7/42
(rule-count unchanged); `--lint-grammar` 0 errors (236 rules); `regex_pcre2_compile_oracle_gate` byte-
identical baseline `2189/1858/285/46`; `duality_hunt_gate` 9 lanes, no new signature; `parse_harness_

## 2026-07-09 - PGEN-REGEX-PCRE2-0022 (REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY.4 SCOPING): the regex out-of-band validator is NOT deletable — tool-backed proof that 8 check families / 54 reject inputs are still LOAD-BEARING; capstone re-scoped into `.4.1`..`.4.11` (PURE-DOCS, no release)

`1.1.91` / schema `1`). On resuming, the `MEMORY.md` next-action framed the capstone `.4` as "delete the

(grammar) FIRST, then `validate_regex_compile_contract` (validator) ONLY if the grammar accepted. So the
rejection MESSAGE names the source: `"Parser did not consume full input"` = grammar rejected (validator
shadowed/dead for that input); a validator `"…compile contract"` string = grammar ACCEPTED and only the
validator rejected (LOAD-BEARING — deleting it makes that input ACCEPT = an accepts-invalid PCRE2
divergence). Ran the validator's OWN pinned reject corpus (its `#[test]` `expect_err` inputs, 58 cases)
through the current release `parseability_probe --parse regex --profile pcre2` (rebuilt this session to
embed the `.3.23` parser) and classified each by message source. Deterministic on re-run. (A first-pass
classifier naively read exit code and mis-reported ALL as "shadowed" — caught immediately as
too-good-to-be-true per the BE-ALERT discipline; the message-source correction gave the true map.)

empty-`\Q\E`-region / orphan-`\E` char-class cases already closed by `.3.15`/`.3.23`). The still-owned
families: bare property escape (`find_invalid_property_escape`), `\k`/group name charset+length ≤128

## 2026-07-08 - PGEN-REGEX-PCRE2-0019 (REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY.3.21): a LIMIT `=value` outside [0, 4294967289] now rejects PCRE2-faithfully; grammar-encoded, regex release 1.1.88

Session #70. A released-parser slice: release `1.1.87`→`1.1.88`, contract `1.1.89`→`1.1.90`,
AST-dump schema stays `1`, ledger `REGEX-0097`. A NEW value-bound closing a latent accepts-invalid
hole (NOT a validator→grammar migration — no validator ever bounded the LIMIT value).

- **The bound (oracle-pinned FIRST, pcre2test 10.47, one-pattern-per-run binary search):** a numeric
  LIMIT start-option value is capped at **4294967289** (`0xFFFFFFF9`); `4294967290` and larger are
  err 160. This is PCRE2's Horner overflow guard (`n > UINT32_MAX/10 - 1` before appending each digit
  ⇒ max = `429496728*10 + 9`), **NOT** u32 max `4294967295` — which itself REJECTS. The leaf's own
  candidate boundary (`4294967295`/`4294967296`) was REFUTED tools-first. Uniform across all 4 LIMIT
  names; purely value-based (unlimited leading zeros; all-zeros = value 0).
- **Divergence.** The released parser (`1.1.87`) accepted ANY digit run — `directive_payload_digits =
  digit+` bounded the SHAPE but no VALUE, and no out-of-band check bounded it (`find_invalid_verb_construct`
  checks name/shape/POSITION only). Latent + hunter-invisible (generator + parser agreed).
- **Grammar encode (tier: GRAMMAR — no engine, no validator):** the `.3.16` `callout_number` /
  `.3.18` `quant_bound_number` STRUCTURAL idiom (NOT `@range` — proved atom-scoped/inert by `.3.16`).
  `directive_payload_digits = directive_limit_value_body -> $text` (wrapper preserving the
  `{separator:"=", value:"<digits>"}` STRING carrier byte-identically); `directive_limit_value_body =
  "0"+ directive_limit_value_core? | directive_limit_value_core`; `directive_limit_value_core` = the
  nonzero-led 1..4294967289 lexicographic ladder. An out-of-range run has NO fully-consuming parse and
  generation is in-range BY CONSTRUCTION. Universal in both profiles (the `.3.18` precedent).
- **Verified.** 21-cell release-probe verdict matrix == pcre2test (0 mismatches, both profiles; the
  out-of-range flips + no fallback hole); AST byte-identical for in-range (`value:"00700"`); generation
  0/601 over-max (seeds 0/7/42); cert `234/234/0 fully_certified spf=0` ×3 seeds (+2 rules witnessed);
  dual suite `892/0`; `duality_hunt_gate` UNCHANGED; `regex_pcre2_compile_oracle_gate` EXACTLY
  byte-identical via decisive stash-baseline (OLD `1858/285/46` == NEW `1858/285/46`). 🔎 The recorded
  oracle baseline `1857/286` was STALE (a `.3.18` universe-shift artifact); corrected to the true
  `1858/285/46`. This closed the last `@range`-class honest bound.

## 2026-07-08 - PGEN-REGEX-PCRE2-0018 (REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY.3.20): only `(*ACCEPT)` may take a quantifier — every other `(*...)` directive quantified now rejects PCRE2-faithfully; grammar-encoded, regex release 1.1.87

Session #69. A released-parser slice: release `1.1.86`→`1.1.87`, contract `1.1.88`→`1.1.89`,
AST-dump schema stays `1`, ledger `REGEX-0096`. The 7th out-of-band-validator → grammar migration.

- **The model (oracle-pinned, pcre2test 10.47; a 30-cell verdict matrix):** PCRE2 makes `(*ACCEPT)`
  the ONLY quantifiable `(*...)` directive — `(*ACCEPT)+` `(*ACCEPT:x)+` `(*ACCEPT){2,3}` ACCEPT —
  while every other form quantified is err 109: the 6 non-ACCEPT verbs (`(*PRUNE)+` `(*FAIL)*` …),
  the `(*:x)` shorthand, MARK (`(*MARK:x)+`), and the start options (`(*UTF)+` `(*UCP)+`
  `(*LIMIT_HEAP=5)+`).
- **Divergence + migration.** The released parser (`1.1.86`) already rejected the verb / shorthand /
  MARK quantified forms (validator-owned) but **latently ACCEPTED `(*UTF)+` / `(*LIMIT_HEAP=5)+`** —
  `find_invalid_verb_construct`'s start-option arm checked POSITION only, never a trailing quantifier.
  This slice both MIGRATES the whole quantified-verb rule out-of-band validator → grammar AND CLOSES
  the start-option-quantified hole (**REGEX-0096**, 2 accepts-invalid flip ACCEPT→REJECT).
- **Grammar encode (tier: GRAMMAR — no engine; validator loses two arms):** `directive_verb` split
  into two atom rules with the SAME `{type:"atom", kind:"directive_verb", body}` carrier —
  `directive_verb` (KEPT in `atom`, quantifiable) = `directive_accept_named | directive_relaxed_named`;
  NEW `directive_verb_nonquant` (a non-quantifiable `piece` branch `directive_verb_nonquant
  !quantifier`, the anchor/`zero_width` idiom) = the 6 non-ACCEPT verbs + MARK + `(*:x)` shorthand +
  LIMIT + bare options. Because `atom` no longer matches a non-ACCEPT directive, a quantified one
  fails the `!quantifier` lookahead AND finds no matching atom ⇒ the whole parse rejects
  err-109-faithfully. `directive_accept_named = "ACCEPT" directive_payload_colon?`; `directive_verb_named`
  re-points to `directive_verb_name_nonaccept` (6 names); the relaxed guard swaps `directive_verb_name`
  for inline `"ACCEPT"` + `directive_verb_name_nonaccept`; the dead `directive_body` / `directive_named`
  / `directive_verb_name` removed (H.10.1 precedent). Validator: the two quantified-verb arms + the dead
  `quantifier_starts_at` helper DELETED; only the start-option POSITION rule stays (capstone `.4`).
- **RELAXED-SEMANTICS decision (within the ratified PCRE2-faithful-by-default + relaxed-opt-out
  principle):** a quantified UNKNOWN-name verb `(*foo)+` stays relaxed-ACCEPTED (relaxed = a strict
  superset that never newly rejects — the unknown-name catch-all is quantifiable), while a KNOWN
  non-ACCEPT directive (`(*PRUNE)+`, `(*UTF)+`, …) rejects in BOTH profiles. Verified on the release
  probe (default vs `--profile relaxed`).
- **AST:** every accepted directive byte-identical (both split rules keep the `directive_verb`
  carrier; `directive_accept_named` keeps `{kind:"named",name,payload}`). Only quantified non-ACCEPT
  directives change verdict. Rejection LAYER moves to `E_PARSE_FAILURE` — match on the **code**.
- **Verified:** 30-cell release-probe verdict matrix == `pcre2test` 10.47 (0 mismatches; both
  start-option divergences now reject); relaxed matrix confirms the decision (`(*foo)+` relaxed-ACCEPT
  / default-REJECT); regex cert **232/232/0** `fully_certified` spf=0 ×seeds 0/7/42 (230→232 = net +2
